takeaway: Extended the KEYNOTE-024 question down to TPS ≥1%. Worth filling in the numbers — the key nuance is that the apparent benefit at TPS 1–49% is largely driven by the TPS ≥50% subgroup.

name: KEYNOTE-045
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma after 1–2 prior lines, ECOG 0–2.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine)
takeaway: Classic ICI pattern — PFS flat or worse, OS clearly better through durable responses. Established pembrolizumab as second-line standard in urothelial carcinoma. Watch the early non-responders who progress fast.

name: KEYNOTE-048
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC; patients with PD within 6 mo after CCRT excluded. Oral cavity 30%, oropharynx 40%, hypopharynx 13%, larynx 25%; TPS ≥50% ~20%, CPS ≥1 ~85%, p16+ 20%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs pembrolizumab + platinum/5-FU vs EXTREME
takeaway: Pembrolizumab-based first-line therapy in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC: monotherapy improves OS in CPS ≥1 and is less toxic but is negative for PFS and ORR. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improves OS and ORR in all patients, with a PFS benefit only in CPS ≥20.

name: KEYNOTE-177
population: Treatment-naive dMMR/MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer. 60% right-sided, 40% RAS/BRAF-mutant.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy (investigator's choice ± bevacizumab/cetuximab)
endpoints: ⚠️ 30% progressed as best response on pembrolizumab
takeaway: Made first-line pembrolizumab standard for dMMR mCRC, with a remarkable 77-month median OS. But 30% have primary resistance and progress immediately — RAS/BRAF-mutant patients may still need chemotherapy, which is the gap CheckMate-8HW's dual blockade addresses.

name: KEYNOTE-181
population: ESCC 64% / adenocarcinoma 36%; one prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemo. Asia 39%; PD-L1 CPS ≥10 in 35%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 2 yr vs taxane or irinotecan (open-label)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab beat chemotherapy on OS only in CPS ≥10, the one co-primary endpoint that met its boundary, and was FDA approved in CPS ≥10. In contrast to ATTRACTION-3, which showed OS benefit regardless of PD-L1.

name: KEYNOTE-189
population: Treatment-naive metastatic NON-SQUAMOUS NSCLC, any PD-L1 level, no EGFR/ALK alteration.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + pemetrexed/platinum vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: The trial that established chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard for non-squamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1. Worth filling in the numbers.

name: KEYNOTE-224 / KEYNOTE-240
population: Child-Pugh A, BCLC B/C HCC.
treatment: Pembrolizumab (n=278) vs placebo (n=135)
endpoints: ⚠️ 3.0 vs 2.8 mo — HR 0.71, P=0.0022 vs boundary 0.002, not met
⚠️ 13.9 vs 10.6 mo — HR 0.78, P=0.0238 vs boundary 0.0174, not met
takeaway: Pembrolizumab numerically favoured OS and PFS in 2L HCC, but neither crossed its statistical boundary (KEYNOTE-240 failed) while ORR was 18.3%. The FDA accelerated approval was maintained (ODAC 2021) and later confirmed by KN-394.

name: KEYNOTE-355
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC, NO CPS requirement for entry. DFI 6–12 mo 20%, >12 mo 50%; de novo metastatic 30%; brain mets 2–6%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + chemo vs placebo + chemo
takeaway: First-line pembrolizumab + chemo improves both PFS and OS — but only at CPS ≥10. Below that, nothing. The sharp contrast with KEYNOTE-522 in early TNBC (where PD-L1 didn't matter at all) is one of the most instructive discrepancies in breast oncology.

name: KEYNOTE-394
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; conducted in Asian countries, HBV-positive.
treatment: Pembrolizumab (n=300) vs placebo (n=153)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab improved OS, PFS and ORR versus placebo in second-line Asian HCC after progression on or intolerance to sorafenib. It confirms the KN-240 signal in an Asian, HBV-predominant population.

name: KEYNOTE-407
population: Treatment-naive metastatic SQUAMOUS NSCLC, any PD-L1 level.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/taxane vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: The squamous counterpart to KEYNOTE-189, establishing chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard regardless of PD-L1. Worth filling in.

name: KEYNOTE-590
population: Both ESCC (73%) and adenocarcinoma (27%). Asia region 53%; PD-L1 CPS ≥10 in 51%. HER2+ excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg + PF vs placebo + PF (double-blind, 1:1)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab plus PF improved PFS, OS and ORR in 1L ESCC/EAC and is the standard of care. Caveat: the benefit is driven by CPS ≥10, with CPS <10 essentially flat (HR 0.86).

name: LEAP-002
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; Asian 40%; Vp4 excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + lenvatinib vs lenvatinib
takeaway: Pembrolizumab + lenvatinib missed prespecified significance for both OS and PFS versus lenvatinib in first-line unresectable HCC. The lenvatinib control arm was strong (mOS 19.0 mo), and the combination was more toxic.

name: MAINTAIN
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (86.5% palbociclib). ≤1 prior chemo line. Not biomarker-selected.
treatment: SWITCHED endocrine therapy + ribociclib vs switched ET + placebo (NSAI → fulvestrant or exemestane)
takeaway: Switching both the endocrine partner AND the CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib → ribociclib) retains benefit after progression — the first randomised evidence for CDK4/6 inhibitor beyond progression. Benefit was significant in ESR1 wild-type; prior CDK4/6i duration ≤12 months may still leave room.

name: MARIPOSA
population: Treatment-naive EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC — Ex19del 60%, L858R 40%. Stable brain mets 40%, with regular brain MRI. Crossover PROHIBITED.
treatment: Amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib vs lazertinib alone — chemotherapy-free
takeaway: A chemo-free amivantamab + lazertinib doublet beat osimertinib on both PFS and OS in first-line EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Watch for toxicity.

name: MARIPOSA-2
population: EGFR Ex19del or L858R NSCLC progressing on or after osimertinib. Stable brain metastases allowed.
treatment: Amivantamab + chemo (± lazertinib) vs chemotherapy alone
endpoints: ⚠️ 17.7 vs 15.3 mo — numerically higher, not mature
takeaway: Addresses the hardest question in EGFR NSCLC — what to do after osimertinib. Amivantamab + chemo improves PFS, ORR and intracranial PFS. Costs: VTE, haematologic and skin toxicity.

name: MetaGIST
population: Unresectable or metastatic GIST on first-line imatinib. Pooled individual-patient data from two phase III trials (EORTC 62005 and SWOG S0033). Median follow-up 45 months; mutation data in 772 patients.
treatment: Imatinib 800 mg/d vs 400 mg/d, first line
takeaway: Upfront high-dose imatinib buys only a small early PFS advantage and no survival benefit — 400 mg remains the standard starting dose. The single exception is KIT exon 9-mutant GIST, where 800 mg more than doubles response rate.

name: ML18147 (TML)
population: mCRC progressing after first-line bevacizumab-containing chemotherapy. Sidedness not analysed. First line was not anti-EGFR.
treatment: Bevacizumab BEYOND progression + second-line chemo vs chemo alone
takeaway: Continuing bevacizumab past progression with a changed chemotherapy backbone improves survival — regardless of tumour sidedness. Established 'bev beyond progression' as a legitimate strategy.

name: MONALEESA-2
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Ribociclib + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole
takeaway: Ribociclib + letrozole delivers both PFS and OS benefit first-line, with median OS exceeding 5 years. Notably, ribociclib has shown OS benefit where palbociclib has not.

name: MONALEESA-3
population: Postmenopausal HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. Half first-line (de novo or relapse >12 mo); half second-line (early relapse ≤12 mo or progression on ET), all CDK4/6i-naive.
treatment: Ribociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Ribociclib works with fulvestrant as well as with an AI, and the OS benefit holds in both first and second line. First-line PFS of 33.6 months is the standout figure.

name: MONALEESA-7
population: PRE/PERI-MENOPAUSAL women with ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. One prior line of chemotherapy allowed. The only CDK4/6 trial dedicated to this group.
treatment: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy + ovarian function suppression vs placebo + ET + OFS
takeaway: The only CDK4/6 inhibitor trial designed specifically for premenopausal women, and it delivered both PFS and OS benefit — nearly doubling PFS.

name: MONARCH-2
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy but CDK4/6i-naive. Any menopausal status; ≤1 prior metastatic chemo line. Primary endocrine resistance in ~25%.
treatment: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant improves PFS and OS after endocrine progression, delaying the move to chemotherapy by well over a year.

name: MONARCH-3
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Abemaciclib + non-steroidal AI vs placebo + NSAI
takeaway: Doubles first-line PFS, and the 13-month numerical OS gain narrowly missed significance. Side effects differ from the other CDK4/6 inhibitors: diarrhoea and VTE dominate over neutropenia.

name: MORPHEUS-Liver
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; Asian 40%. Small cohorts: 40 vs 18 patients.
treatment: A+B + tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) (n=40) vs A+B (n=18)
takeaway: Adding tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) to A+B improved ORR, PFS and OS in this phase Ib/II first-line unresectable HCC study, but the numbers are small (40 vs 18) with an underperforming control arm. The confirmatory IMbrave152/SKYSCRAPER-14 trial failed.

name: MOUNTAINEER
population: RAS wild-type, HER2-positive chemorefractory mCRC. Median 2–3 prior lines. Prior anti-HER2 excluded.
treatment: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (vs tucatinib alone)
takeaway: Tucatinib + trastuzumab is active and well tolerated in HER2+ RAS wild-type refractory mCRC — a 24-month median OS in a heavily pretreated population. Led to FDA approval.

name: MVAC (Loehrer)
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma, cisplatin-eligible.
treatment: MVAC vs single-agent cisplatin
takeaway: The trial that established combination chemotherapy in urothelial carcinoma — more than tripling response rate over single-agent cisplatin. The foundation everything since has been measured against.

name: MyPathway (HER2 CRC cohort)
population: HER2-amplified mCRC, median 4 prior lines. Prior anti-HER2 excluded.
treatment: Trastuzumab + pertuzumab (single-arm basket)
takeaway: Dual HER2 antibody blockade is active and well tolerated in HER2-amplified mCRC, particularly in KRAS wild-type. The short PFS reflects how heavily pretreated these patients were.

name: NALA
population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer after ≥2 prior HER2-directed regimens. ECOG 0–1, 59% HR+, 84% visceral, 16.6% baseline brain mets. Prior: 99.7% trastuzumab, 42% pertuzumab, 54% T-DM1.
treatment: Neratinib + capecitabine vs lapatinib + capecitabine
endpoints: ✅ Fewer CNS interventions 22.8% vs 29.2%, P=0.043; DoR 8.5 vs 5.6 mo
takeaway: The first TKI-versus-TKI superiority trial in metastatic breast cancer. Note the tell-tale pattern — identical median PFS but separated mean PFS, meaning the benefit is in the tail. Grade 3 diarrhoea in 24% despite prophylaxis.

name: NO16966
population: Previously untreated mCRC, ECOG ≤1.
treatment: Bevacizumab + oxaliplatin-based chemo (FOLFOX4 or XELOX) vs chemo alone
takeaway: Bevacizumab improved PFS but not OS or response rate with an oxaliplatin backbone — a weaker effect than with irinotecan. A key subtlety: many patients stopped bevacizumab early for chemo toxicity, which is why the trial argues for continuing bevacizumab until progression.

name: NSABP-B27 (real-world, Jordan)
population: 346 women with high-risk early breast cancer treated neoadjuvantly in Jordan 2003–2014. Median tumour 6.0 cm; 78.3% node-positive — notably more advanced than the original B-27 trial.
treatment: AC ×4 → docetaxel ×4 (single arm)
takeaway: Real-world outcomes matched the trial (pCR 25% vs 26%) despite larger tumours and far more nodal involvement. HR-negative, node-negative and smaller tumours predicted higher pCR. Note: this row sits in your Metastatic DB but is an early-stage neoadjuvant study — it may belong in the Early DB.

name: OlympiAD
population: Germline BRCA1/2-mutant, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, ≤2 prior metastatic chemo lines. Prior anthracycline and taxane required; prior platinum for metastatic disease EXCLUDED.
treatment: Olaparib vs physician's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: First PARP inhibitor trial in breast cancer — PFS benefit, no OS. But an OS signal in the chemotherapy-naive subgroup pointed toward earlier use, which is exactly what OlympiA went on to prove in the adjuvant setting.

name: P025
population: Postmenopausal advanced breast cancer, HR-positive (65%) or unknown (35%). Prior adjuvant endocrine therapy allowed.
treatment: Letrozole vs tamoxifen, first-line for advanced disease
takeaway: Established aromatase inhibitors over tamoxifen as first-line endocrine therapy in advanced disease — the metastatic counterpart to ATAC and BIG 1-98.

name: PALOMA-2
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Palbociclib + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole
takeaway: Palbociclib clearly extends PFS but — unlike ribociclib in MONALEESA-2 — never delivered an OS benefit. The central unexplained puzzle of the CDK4/6 class. Main toxicity is myelosuppression.

name: PALOMA-3
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy, CDK4/6i-naive. Any menopausal status; ≤1 prior metastatic chemo line. Primary endocrine resistance ~21%.
treatment: Palbociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Doubles PFS after endocrine progression. The OS story is subgroup-dependent: no ITT benefit, but a large one in endocrine-sensitive patients — prior endocrine sensitivity predicts who gains.

name: PAOLA-1
population: FIGO III–IV high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer after first-line platinum-taxane + bevacizumab, regardless of surgical outcome or HRD status. CR 20%, stage III 70%, BRCA-mutant 30%, HRD-positive ~50%.
treatment: Maintenance olaparib 300 mg BID × 2 years + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w × 15 months vs placebo + bevacizumab
takeaway: Olaparib + bevacizumab maintenance after first-line platinum-taxane + bevacizumab improved PFS and OS in HRD-positive ovarian cancer — the only PARP inhibitor with an OS benefit. HRD-negative patients gain no PFS or OS benefit.

name: PARADIGM
population: RAS wild-type mCRC, ECOG 0–1, prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded. Primary analysis in LEFT-SIDED tumours.
treatment: Panitumumab vs bevacizumab, both with mFOLFOX6
takeaway: The definitive prospective answer to the sidedness question — anti-EGFR first in LEFT-sided RAS wild-type disease, anti-VEGF for right-sided. Depth of response correlated with better OS.

name: PARSIFAL
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, ENDOCRINE-SENSITIVE, no prior treatment for advanced disease. Prior perioperative ET allowed if DFS >12 months.
treatment: Fulvestrant + palbociclib vs letrozole + palbociclib
endpoints: ❌ 27.9 vs 32.8 mo — HR 1.13 (0.89–1.45), P=0.32 — superiority NOT shown
takeaway: Fulvestrant is not a better CDK4/6 partner than an aromatase inhibitor in endocrine-sensitive first-line disease. Keep the NSAI.

name: postMONARCH
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (60% palbociclib), in either the advanced or early setting. Prior metastatic chemotherapy excluded. Not biomarker-selected.
treatment: SWITCHED endocrine therapy (AI → fulvestrant) + abemaciclib vs switched ET + placebo
takeaway: Confirms in phase III what MAINTAIN suggested — CDK4/6 inhibition beyond progression works, without biomarker selection. Unlike MAINTAIN, prior CDK4/6i duration did not affect the benefit. Be realistic about magnitude: the median PFS gain is under a month.

name: PRIME
population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC, ECOG ≤2. Prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded.
treatment: Panitumumab + FOLFOX4 vs FOLFOX4
takeaway: Panitumumab + FOLFOX improves both PFS and OS — but only in fully RAS wild-type tumours. The extended RAS analysis of this trial is what expanded testing beyond KRAS exon 2.

name: PYNNACLE
population: Solid tumours carrying the TP53 Y220C mutation (ovary, pancreas, breast, CRC, endometrial, lung, HEENT and others). ECOG 0–1, median 3 prior lines.
treatment: Rezatapopt (PC14586), an oral selective p53 reactivator (single-arm)
endpoints: 20% overall; 30% in KRAS wild-type at ≥1150 mg
takeaway: Proof of concept that a mutant p53 protein can be pharmacologically reactivated — a target considered undruggable for decades. RP2D 2000 mg daily with food; main toxicities GI and anaemia.

name: RAINBOW
population: Metastatic gastric or EGJ (20%) adenocarcinoma only, after prior platinum-fluoropyrimidine. Asian 34%; peritoneal mets 47%.
treatment: Ramucirumab + paclitaxel vs placebo + paclitaxel (no crossover)
takeaway: Ramucirumab + paclitaxel improved PFS, OS and ORR over placebo + paclitaxel in second-line metastatic gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma, and it is the only antiangiogenic to succeed in GC/EGJ. The benefit was larger in EGJ adenocarcinoma (OS HR 0.521) than in gastric cancer (HR 0.899).

name: RASolute 302
population: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0–1, ≥1 prior fluoropyrimidine/gemcitabine chemotherapy, RAS-mutant. Asian ~10%; ECOG 0 50%; RAS G12X ~100%.
treatment: Daraxonrasib 300 mg PO QD vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: Daraxonrasib improved PFS, OS and ORR over investigator's-choice chemotherapy in ≥2L metastatic pancreatic cancer. Median OS of 13.2 mo in the second-line setting is the headline.

name: RATIONALE-301
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; Vp4 status not specified.
treatment: Tislelizumab vs sorafenib (non-inferiority design)
takeaway: Tislelizumab was non-inferior to sorafenib for OS in 1L unresectable HCC, but PFS was worse. It had a higher ORR and far fewer ≥Gr3 TRAEs.

name: RATIONALE-302
population: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma only, after one prior chemotherapy line. 79% Asia. PD-L1 TAP ≥10% in 31%.
treatment: Tislelizumab 200 mg q3w vs taxane or irinotecan (open-label, 1:1)
endpoints: ❌ 1.6 vs 2.1 mo — HR 0.83 (0.67–1.01); ⚠️ but 12-mo PFS 12.7% vs 1.9% (curves separate after ~3 mo)
takeaway: Tislelizumab improved OS but not PFS versus chemotherapy in second-line ESCC (PFS 1.6 vs 2.1 months, though the curves separate after ~3 months). The benefit is concentrated in PD-L1-positive (TAP ≥10%) patients.

name: RATIONALE-306
population: ESCC only; 75% Asian; 44% had prior definitive therapy; PD-L1 TAP ≥10% in 34%.
treatment: Tislelizumab + chemo (PF or TP) vs placebo + chemo (double-blind, 1:1, N=649)
takeaway: Tislelizumab + chemotherapy improved PFS, OS and ORR over chemotherapy alone in first-line ESCC. The benefit was driven by TAP ≥10%; the TAP <10% subgroup did not reach significance (HR 0.77, CI crossing 1).

name: RATIONALE-309
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC; all Asian, China only. Liver mets ~40%, baseline EBV-positive ~80%, 75% prior CCRT.
treatment: Tislelizumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin (GP) vs placebo + GP; induction then maintenance; 49% crossover
endpoints: 69.5% vs 55.3% (BICR); 77.9% vs 67.4% (investigator); mDoR 8.5 vs 6.1 mo (BICR), 10.6 vs 6.2 mo (investigator)
takeaway: Tislelizumab added to gemcitabine/cisplatin improved PFS in first-line recurrent/metastatic NPC, but OS was not significant, with 49% crossover as the likely confounder. The row notes it as the only TFDA-approved option.

name: FOLFOXIRI — GONO
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age 62. ECOG 0–1 in 98% — a deliberately FIT population.
treatment: FOLFOXIRI vs FOLFIRI (oxaliplatin 85, irinotecan 165, infusional 5-FU 46 h)
takeaway: Triplet chemotherapy improves response, PFS and OS — but only in genuinely fit patients (98% were ECOG 0–1). Patient selection is the whole story; see the HORG trial for what happens without it.

name: FOLFOXIRI — HORG
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age 66, age ≥75 permitted. ECOG 0 in only 36%, ECOG 2 in 11%. Crossover allowed.
treatment: FOLFOXIRI vs FOLFIRI (lower doses: oxaliplatin 65, irinotecan 150, bolus 5-FU)
takeaway: The negative mirror image of the GONO trial — an older, less fit population, lower drug doses and bolus 5-FU produced no benefit and heavy toxicity. Together the two trials define exactly who FOLFOXIRI is for.

name: REACH-2
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; AFP >400; progression on sorafenib.
treatment: Ramucirumab (n=197) vs placebo (n=95)
takeaway: Ramucirumab improved OS and PFS versus placebo in second-line HCC with AFP ≥400. Benefit is restricted to AFP ≥400, as REACH-1 (all-comers) was negative.

name: RECOURSE
population: Refractory mCRC, median 3 prior regimens, 20% prior regorafenib. ECOG 0 in ~56%.
treatment: Trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) vs placebo
takeaway: Established TAS-102 as a third-line option in refractory mCRC. Like regorafenib, the benefit is real but small — disease stabilisation rather than response.

name: REFLECT
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C HCC. Excluded Vp4, bile duct invasion and tumor >50% of the liver.
treatment: Lenvatinib (n=478) vs sorafenib (n=476); non-inferiority design
takeaway: Lenvatinib was non-inferior to sorafenib for OS in 1L unresectable HCC, with better PFS and ORR. Eligibility excluded Vp4, bile duct invasion and ≥50% liver occupation, so the results apply to a selected population.

name: RESORCE
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, progression on sorafenib; patients had to tolerate sorafenib.
treatment: Regorafenib (n=379) vs placebo (n=194)
takeaway: Regorafenib improved OS and PFS over placebo in 2L HCC after sorafenib and was the first 2L approval. Caveat: only patients who tolerated sorafenib were enrolled.

name: ReTrITA
population: Refractory mCRC after ≥2 prior lines.
treatment: Sequencing study — regorafenib → TAS-102 vs TAS-102 → regorafenib
endpoints: ✅ 11.5 vs 8.5 mo — HR 0.60 (0.49–0.74), P<0.0001 (monotherapy PFS nearly identical: 3.2 vs 3.3 mo)
takeaway: Sequence matters — regorafenib first, then TAS-102. Note the tell: each drug's individual PFS is identical, so the benefit comes from the ordering, not from either agent. Retrospective, so treat with appropriate caution.

name: RIGHT Choice
population: PRE/PERI-MENOPAUSAL women with aggressive HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer — including visceral crisis — with no prior treatment for advanced disease. The population clinicians reflexively give chemotherapy.
treatment: Ribociclib + NSAI + ovarian function suppression vs investigator's-choice combination chemotherapy
takeaway: Directly challenges the instinct to reach for chemotherapy in visceral crisis — endocrine therapy plus ribociclib gave 9 months more PFS with better tolerability. Practice-changing for aggressive premenopausal HR+ disease.

name: RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib, CRC)
population: RAS-mutant refractory colorectal cancer (details not yet captured).
treatment: RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib) — RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder for the colorectal cohort of daraxonrasib. Worth filling in — the same drug produced a doubling of OS in pancreatic cancer (RASolute 302).

name: Saltz et al.
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age ~60. Over half were ECOG 1–2; 80% had liver metastases.
treatment: Irinotecan + 5-FU/LV (IFL) vs 5-FU/LV vs irinotecan alone
takeaway: The trial that moved metastatic colorectal cancer from single-agent fluorouracil to doublet chemotherapy, lifting response rates from ~20% to 50%. The starting point of the modern mCRC treatment sequence.

name: SERENA-6
population: ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with an EMERGENT ESR1 mutation detected on ctDNA surveillance during first-line AI + CDK4/6i (≥6 months), with NO radiographic progression yet. A genuinely novel entry criterion.
treatment: Switch to camizestrant + continue the same CDK4/6 inhibitor vs continue AI + CDK4/6i
takeaway: The first trial to act on a molecular relapse before it becomes a radiographic one — switching endocrine partner on emergent ESR1 ctDNA nearly doubles PFS while keeping the CDK4/6 inhibitor. A new treatment paradigm, though OS is not yet known.

name: SHARP
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤2; >80% from Europe and Australasia.
treatment: Sorafenib (n=299) vs placebo (n=303)
takeaway: Sorafenib improved OS and PFS versus placebo in first-line advanced HCC, making it the first systemic standard of care. ORR was about 0%, so the benefit comes from stable disease (DCR 43% vs 32%).

name: SOFT (adjuvant)
population: Pre/perimenopausal women with HR+ early breast cancer — adjuvant setting.
treatment: Tamoxifen alone vs tamoxifen + OFS vs exemestane + OFS
takeaway: High-risk premenopausal women benefit from ovarian function suppression. Note: this row sits in your Metastatic DB but is an adjuvant trial, and largely duplicates the SOFT/TEXT entry in your Early DB — worth consolidating.

name: SOHO-01
population: HER2-mutant NSCLC (details not yet captured).
treatment: Sevabertinib (BAY 2927088) — HER2-selective TKI
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder for sevabertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC — a sibling to zongertinib (Beamion Lung-01). Worth filling both in together for comparison.

name: SOLAR-1
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, men and postmenopausal women, relapsed/progressed on an AI; no chemo in the advanced setting; prior CDK4/6i 6%. Primary analysis in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort; patients with diabetes/poor glycaemic control excluded.
treatment: Alpelisib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Alpelisib + fulvestrant improved PFS but not OS in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after an AI. Bone-only disease seemed not to benefit, and severe hyperglycaemia was a notable toxicity.

name: Sorafenib in desmoid tumour
population: Progressive, symptomatic or recurrent desmoid tumours. Median age 37, 69% female, 40% prior systemic therapy, 50% prior surgery. Crossover allowed at progression.
treatment: Sorafenib 400 mg daily vs placebo
endpoints: ✅ 33% vs 20% — median time to response 9.6 mo
takeaway: First randomised phase III in desmoid tumours, with a striking 87% reduction in progression risk. Two clinical lessons: responses are late (median 9.6 months) so don't abandon stable disease early, and the 20% placebo response rate supports watchful waiting as a first move. 20% discontinued for skin toxicity.

name: STELLAR-303
population: MSS/pMMR refractory mCRC — a true third line: all had received 5-FU, irinotecan and oxaliplatin; no prior regorafenib, TAS-102 or ICI; BRAF-mutant required prior BRAF-targeted therapy.
treatment: Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab vs regorafenib
takeaway: Immunotherapy finally shows an OS signal in MSS colorectal cancer — but with a modest 1.5-month gain and substantially more toxicity. Weigh carefully in a late-line population.

name: SUNLIGHT
population: Refractory mCRC — >90% had exactly 2 prior lines. ECOG 0 in 43–48%.
treatment: TAS-102 + bevacizumab vs TAS-102 alone
endpoints: ✅ No prior bev HR 0.40 vs prior bev HR 0.72
takeaway: Adding bevacizumab to TAS-102 more than doubles PFS and gives a 3.3-month OS gain — the best third-line result in mCRC. Benefit is much larger in bevacizumab-naive patients.

name: TRIBE
population: All-comer mCRC, unselected for RAS/BRAF or sidedness. ECOG 0 in ~90%; right-sided 25–35%.
treatment: Bevacizumab + FOLFOXIRI (triplet) vs bevacizumab + FOLFIRI (doublet)
takeaway: Triplet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab improves OS in fit patients. Subgroup analysis supports it particularly for right-sided tumours, where anti-EGFR does not work.

name: TRIBE2
population: All-comer mCRC, unselected for RAS/BRAF or sidedness. ECOG 0 in ~85%; right-sided 40%.
treatment: Upfront bevacizumab-triplet (with reintroduction after progression) vs sequential bevacizumab-doublet
takeaway: Confirms TRIBE with a strategy endpoint — giving the triplet upfront, then reintroducing it, beats sequential doublets on PFS2 and OS. Particularly relevant for right-sided disease.

name: TriComB
population: UNFIT, elderly mCRC — median age 80, ECOG 1 in ~55%, RAS-mutant ~80%.
treatment: TAS-102 + capecitabine + bevacizumab
takeaway: A chemo-light triplet for patients too frail for standard doublets — 55% response and 10 months PFS at a median age of 80 is a strong early signal. Randomised confirmation pending.

name: TRIPLETE
population: RAS/BRAF wild-type mCRC, left-sided 88%, ECOG 0 in ~80%. Prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded.
treatment: Panitumumab + FOLFOXIRI vs panitumumab + FOLFOX
endpoints: ✅ 41.1 vs 33.3 mo — HR 0.79 (0.63–0.99), P=0.049 — inconsistent with the primary result
takeaway: In RAS/BRAF wild-type disease, anti-EGFR plus a doublet is already good enough — the triplet adds toxicity without improving response or PFS. Treat the borderline OS finding with scepticism given the negative primary endpoint.

name: TROPION-Breast02
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC, ICI-INELIGIBLE. No DFI requirement — deliberately includes the worst-prognosis first-line patients: DFI 0–6 mo 15%, de novo 34%, brain mets 10%.
treatment: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: First-line Dato-DXd improves BOTH PFS and OS in ICI-ineligible metastatic TNBC — and did so in a deliberately poor-prognosis population (the highest brain-met and short-DFI proportions of any first-line TNBC trial). Sits alongside ASCENT-03 as the answer for CPS <10 disease.

name: VIKTORIA-1
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, PIK3CA wild-type, progressed on CDK4/6i + NSAI.
treatment: Gedatolisib + fulvestrant ± palbociclib vs fulvestrant (open-label)
endpoints: ✅ 9.3 (triplet) vs 7.4 (doublet) vs 2.0 (fulvestrant) — triplet HR 0.24 (0.17–0.35), P<0.001; doublet HR 0.33 (0.24–0.48), P<0.001
⚠️ 23.7 (triplet) vs 18.5 (fulvestrant), HR 0.69 (0.43–1.12); doublet NR vs 18.5, HR 0.74 (0.46–1.19)
takeaway: In PIK3CA wild-type HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6i + NSAI, gedatolisib + fulvestrant with or without palbociclib improved PFS. OS is not yet conclusive, and the triplet causes neutropenia.

name: ATTRACTION-5
population: Pathological stage IIIA–C gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after gastrectomy with D2+ lymph-node dissection. Asian only (Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China).
treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab + chemotherapy vs placebo + chemotherapy
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab added to chemotherapy did not improve RFS after D2 gastrectomy for stage III gastric/GEJ cancer. It is the first phase 3 of adjuvant ICI after D2 surgery in Asia and it is negative, in contrast with the perioperative approaches tested in KEYNOTE-585 and MATTERHORN. The nivolumab arm paid for it in toxicity — endocrine adverse events 21% vs 3% and more discontinuations — with no efficacy in return.

name: CheckMate-141
population: Recurrent/metastatic HNSCC progressing within 6 months of platinum given either as adjuvant therapy or as first-line treatment for metastatic disease. Oral cavity 50%, oropharynx 35%, larynx 14%. Prior cetuximab 62%, ≥2 prior lines 55%, PD-L1 ≥1% 57%.
treatment: Nivolumab monotherapy vs investigator's choice (methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab), randomised 2:1
takeaway: Nivolumab monotherapy improves overall survival in platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic HNSCC without improving PFS — the gain is in the tail of the curve, not the early one. Benefit is concentrated in PD-L1-positive disease and vanishes below 1%. Its entry criteria were broader than KEYNOTE-040's: patients recurring within 3 months of definitive platinum-based therapy were eligible here.

name: CheckMate-238
population: Completely resected (R0) stage IIIB, IIIC or IV cutaneous melanoma (AJCC7); stage IIIA excluded. Resected brain metastases allowed (24% with brain mets in stage IV). IIIB 35%, IIIC 45%, IV ~20%; BRAF-mutant 40%.
treatment: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w vs ipilimumab 10 mg/kg q3w ×4 then q12w (both up to 1 year)
endpoints: ↔ 9-yr 69% vs 65%, median NR (>9 yr) in both — HR 0.88 (95.03% CI 0.69–1.11); melanoma-specific HR 0.87 (0.67–1.13)
PD-L1 <5% HR 0.71, ≥5% HR 0.50; stage III HR 0.65, stage IV HR 0.70
takeaway: One year of adjuvant nivolumab improved RFS and DMFS over ipilimumab and is the standard of care, with far less toxicity than ipilimumab. OS showed no difference, which the row attributes to the active comparator.

name: CheckMate-511
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III–IV melanoma. Prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 wk earlier; active brain mets excluded.
treatment: NIVO3 + IPI1 ×4 vs NIVO1 + IPI3 ×4, then nivolumab 480 mg q4w maintenance
endpoints: ↔ NR vs NR; 12-mo 79.7% vs 81.0% — HR 1.09 (0.73–1.62), descriptive
57.3% vs 62.4% — calculated, not reported as DCR in the paper
takeaway: Switching from NIVO1 + IPI3 (as used in CM-067) to NIVO3 + IPI1 gave a better safety profile with similar efficacy, meeting the primary endpoint of lower grade 3–5 treatment-related adverse events. Efficacy endpoints are descriptive only, and there was no comparison to nivolumab monotherapy.

name: CheckMate-76K
population: Resected stage IIB or IIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 8th), no treatment other than surgery; ocular and mucosal melanoma excluded. IIB 60%; superficial spreading 30%, nodular 50%, acral 5%; BRAF V600E-mutant 28–30%.
treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg q4w × 1 yr vs placebo, randomised 2:1
endpoints: ⚠️ New primary melanomas COUNTED as RFS events and death COUNTED as a DMFS event — unlike KEYNOTE-716
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab for 1 year more than halves the recurrence hazard in resected stage IIB–IIC melanoma, with a matching distant-metastasis benefit. There is still no OS report, and the price is real: 50% discontinued for adverse events and 15% needed hormone replacement for endocrine immune toxicity. Because it counts new primary melanomas as RFS events where KEYNOTE-716 does not, the two trials' hazard ratios are not directly comparable.

name: CheckMate-915
population: Completely resected stage IIIB–D or IV melanoma (AJCC 8th); complete lymph-node dissection NOT required. Cutaneous ~88%, acral ~3%, mucosal ~1%; stage IV 13%; BRAF-mutant 31%.
treatment: Nivolumab 240 mg q2w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w vs nivolumab 480 mg q4w + placebo — both ≤1 year
endpoints: ⚠️ 2-yr 89.8% vs 91.8% — HR 1.09 (0.80–1.32), immature and numerically favours nivolumab alone
takeaway: Adding low-dose ipilimumab to adjuvant nivolumab failed both co-primary RFS endpoints and DMFS, with immature OS running numerically the wrong way — single-agent nivolumab, as in CheckMate-238, is enough. The one useful design lesson is that enrolling patients who had not had a completion lymph-node dissection did not degrade RFS.

name: COMBI-AD
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th) carrying a BRAF V600E (90%) or V600K mutation. IIIB 40%, IIIC 40%.
treatment: Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg QD × 1 yr vs placebo
endpoints: ⚠️ 3-yr 86% vs 77% — HR 0.57 (0.42–0.79), P=0.0006 against a required P=0.000019, so not significant
takeaway: One year of adjuvant dabrafenib/trametinib halves the recurrence hazard and improves DMFS in resected BRAF V600-mutant stage III melanoma; OS improved numerically but never crossed the extremely stringent interim boundary. It makes targeted therapy a legitimate adjuvant option in BRAF-mutant disease — but DREAMseq later showed that in the metastatic setting ICI should come before BRAF/MEK inhibition.

name: DREAMseq
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III or IV melanoma with BRAF V600E/K mutation (V600E 82%, V600K 12%). Excluded any prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4 or BRAF/MEK therapy, even in the neo/adjuvant setting (prior adjuvant 12–16%); treated brain mets allowed.
treatment: Sequence A/C: nivolumab + ipilimumab first, then dabrafenib/trametinib after PD. Sequence B/D: dabrafenib/trametinib first, then nivolumab + ipilimumab after PD. Nivo-ipi always followed by maintenance nivolumab
endpoints: ✅ Dab/tram 2L ORR 47.8% vs nivo/ipi 2L 29.6%; mPFS 9.9 vs 2.9 mo
takeaway: In BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma, nivolumab + ipilimumab should precede BRAF/MEK inhibition, with benefit in OS, duration of response and 2L ORR. The benefit comes from the second line: TKIs still work after dual ICI, but dual ICI works poorly after a TKI; with crossover in only 50%, first-line therapy matters most.

name: EORTC 18071
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th); LDH >2× ULN excluded. IIIB 40%, IIIC 40%. BRAF status not prespecified.
treatment: Ipilimumab 10 mg/kg q3w ×4 then q12w for up to 3 years vs placebo
takeaway: The first adjuvant melanoma trial to show an overall survival benefit, proving that adjuvant checkpoint blockade can do more than delay recurrence. It is a landmark rather than a current option: high-dose ipilimumab was so toxic that the median patient received only 4 doses of a planned 3-year course, and it was superseded by adjuvant nivolumab in CheckMate-238.

name: EXTREME
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC with detectable EGFR expression.
treatment: Platinum + 5-FU + cetuximab (400 → 250 mg/m² weekly) vs platinum + 5-FU alone; chemotherapy q3w for up to 6 cycles
takeaway: Adding cetuximab to platinum/5-FU improved response, PFS and overall survival, making it the first-line standard of care in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC until KEYNOTE-048 displaced it. The cost is more sepsis and hypomagnesaemia.

name: INFINITY
population: Resectable dMMR/MSI-H, EBV-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (Italian GONO). Cohort 1 (n=18) cT≥2 any N M0 proceeds to surgery; cohort 2 (n=18) cT2–3 any N M0 goes to definitive non-operative management if a clinical CR is achieved (T4 excluded after cohort 1).
treatment: Chemo-free tremelimumab 300 mg ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w ×3 (T300/D), single arm
endpoints: ⚠️ Single-arm — no DFS, no hazard ratios
takeaway: Chemo-free neoadjuvant tremelimumab + durvalumab produced a 60% pCR and 80% major pathological response in resectable MSI-H gastric/GEJ cancer, reproducing NEONIPIGA. Cohort 2 provides the first prospective feasibility data for organ preservation in this disease — 76% reached a clinical CR and avoided surgery, with a single local regrowth salvaged surgically. T4 tumours respond far less well (pCR 17% vs 89%), linked to an M2-macrophage-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment, and are now excluded from the non-operative cohort.

name: INT-0099
population: Stage III–IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma (AJCC/UICC), no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, performance status 0–2.
treatment: Concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation → adjuvant cisplatin/5-FU vs radiotherapy alone
endpoints: ✅ NR vs 15 mo; 3-yr 66% vs 26% — HR 4.34 (2.47–7.69) for RT alone vs chemoradiation, P<0.001
✅ NR vs 34 mo; 3-yr 76% vs 46% — HR 2.50 (1.29–4.84) for RT alone vs chemoradiation, P=0.005
takeaway: The landmark trial that made concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation followed by adjuvant chemotherapy the standard of care in stage III–IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma, roughly doubling 3-year PFS and OS over radiotherapy alone. Read the hazard ratios carefully: they are expressed with radiotherapy alone in the numerator, so values above 1 favour chemoradiation.

name: KEYNOTE-585
population: Untreated, locally advanced, resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (T3 or deeper, or node-positive, M0). Global — 143 centres in 24 countries, 47% Asia.
treatment: Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab + chemotherapy vs placebo + chemotherapy on a cisplatin/capecitabine or 5-FU backbone (separate FLOT safety cohort, n=203)
endpoints: ⚠️ 44.4 vs 25.3 mo — HR 0.81 (0.67–0.99), P=0.0198 against a boundary of P<0.0178, so not met; 2-yr EFS 58% vs 51%
takeaway: Perioperative pembrolizumab produced a large pCR gain but missed the prespecified EFS significance boundary by a hair (P=0.0198 vs the required 0.0178), and OS was not significant. It is the first global phase 3 of perioperative ICI in resectable gastric/GEJ cancer and a near-miss, contrasting with the subsequently positive MATTERHORN. The main cohort did not use FLOT as the chemotherapy backbone, which limits how far the result travels outside Asia.

name: KEYNOTE-040
population: Recurrent/metastatic HNSCC progressing on platinum, or recurring within 3–6 months of platinum-based definitive therapy — a narrower population than CheckMate-141. Prior cetuximab 60%, ≥2 prior lines ~30%, PD-L1 ≥1% 80%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs investigator's choice (methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab); crossover 13%
takeaway: Pembrolizumab monotherapy improved overall survival in platinum-refractory, PD-L1-positive HNSCC but not PFS or response rate. The benefit is largest at TPS ≥50% and absent below CPS 1 (HR 1.28). Its eligible population was narrower than CheckMate-141's, admitting recurrence 3–6 months after definitive therapy.

name: KEYNOTE-054
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th). IIIA 15%, IIIB 45%, IIIC 37%; BRAF V600-mutant 40–45%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 18 doses (~1 yr) vs placebo
takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab became a standard of care in resected stage III melanoma, cutting the recurrence hazard by roughly 43% with a matching distant-metastasis benefit, and it works regardless of PD-L1 status. OS is still immature, and — unlike CheckMate-238 — no stage IV patients were enrolled, so the result does not extend to resected metastatic disease.

name: KEYNOTE-716
population: Resected stage IIB or IIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 8th), no treatment other than surgery. IIB 65%. Histological subtype and BRAF status were deliberately not prespecified for subgroup analysis.
treatment: Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 1 yr vs placebo
endpoints: ⚠️ New primary melanomas NOT counted as RFS events and death NOT counted as a DMFS event — unlike CheckMate-76K
takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab improves RFS and DMFS in resected stage IIB–IIC melanoma, the stage-II counterpart to CheckMate-76K. Check the endpoint definitions before comparing the two: this trial excluded new primary melanomas from RFS events and deaths from DMFS events, where CheckMate-76K counted both. OS is immature, and BRAF and PD-L1 subgroups were deliberately not prespecified.

name: NADINA
population: Stage IIIB–IIID melanoma (AJCC 8th) with clinically overt nodal disease. Unknown primary 20%, in-transit metastases 10%; T2 20%, T3 20%, T4 25%; BRAF-mutant 50%.
treatment: Perioperative nivolumab 240 mg + ipilimumab 80 mg q3w ×2 → therapeutic lymph node dissection → response-driven therapy (nothing further after a major pathological response; dabrafenib/trametinib ×46 wk if BRAF-mutant, nivolumab ×11 if wild-type) vs adjuvant control (TLND → nivolumab 480 mg q4w ×12)
endpoints: ✅ pCR 47.2% + near-pCR 11.8% = MPR 59.0%; by BRAF, mutant 53.8% vs wild-type 65.3%; radiologic ORR at wk 6 35.8%
⏳ Blinded until the prespecified final analysis, 3 years after the last patient is enrolled
takeaway: Two cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab/ipilimumab before lymph node dissection cut the event hazard by two-thirds versus standard adjuvant nivolumab, and 59% of patients achieved a major pathological response and needed no further therapy at all. It also establishes pathological response as predictive of survival — 12-month RFS runs from 95% in major responders down to 57% in non-responders — which is what makes response-driven escalation and de-escalation possible. OS is still blinded.

name: NEONIPIGA
population: Resectable dMMR/MSI-H gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2–T4 N0/1 M0, ECOG 0–1, age ≤75; French GERCOR study across 11 centres.
treatment: Neoadjuvant nivolumab + low-dose ipilimumab → surgery → adjuvant nivolumab (single arm)
endpoints: Not reached at 14.9-mo median follow-up; 30/31 (97%) eligible patients alive and event-free (1 postoperative death)
Not reached; 30/31 (97%) alive at data cutoff
⚠️ Single-arm — no DFS, no hazard ratios
takeaway: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab produced a 58.6% pCR in resectable dMMR/MSI-H gastric/GEJ cancer, far above the ~3–11% historically achieved with chemotherapy, with 100% R0 resection and manageable immune-related toxicity. It raised the question of a watch-and-wait, non-operative strategy for MSI-H gastric cancer, tested prospectively in INFINITY cohort 2. Neither PD-L1 CPS nor Lynch-versus-sporadic status predicted pathological response.

name: PRODIGY
population: Korean, ECOG 0–1, cT2–3 node-positive or cT4 any N gastric cancer (AJCC 7th). Stage III 80%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant DOS (docetaxel/oxaliplatin/S-1) ×3 → surgery → adjuvant S-1 vs surgery → adjuvant S-1
endpoints: 10.4% (23/222) in the neoadjuvant arm; not applicable to the surgery-first arm
⚠️ 3-yr 74.2% vs 73.4% — HR 0.84 (0.60–1.19), P=0.338; immature and underpowered
takeaway: The first Asian phase 3 to show that adding neoadjuvant chemotherapy to surgery plus adjuvant S-1 improves progression-free survival in locally advanced gastric cancer. The gain did not carry through to overall survival — the OS analysis was immature and underpowered — so it supports rather than proves the perioperative approach in a D2-gastrectomy population.

name: RELATIVITY-047
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III or IV melanoma. Prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 months earlier; active CNS mets excluded. BRAF mutant 38%.
treatment: Relatlimab 160 mg + nivolumab 480 mg vs nivolumab (Q4W)
takeaway: Relatlimab + nivolumab improved PFS, ORR and OS over nivolumab alone, and this was the first positive LAG-3 trial. PD-L1 was not predictive of efficacy.

name: SWOG S1801
population: Resectable stage IIIB–IIID or oligometastatic stage IV melanoma (AJCC 8th) with clinically overt nodal disease (resectable node >1.5 cm short axis). Prior ICI and brain metastases excluded. IIIB 40%, IIIC 45%; acral 3%, mucosal 3%; BRAF-mutant ~25%.
treatment: Perioperative pembrolizumab ×3 → surgery → pembrolizumab ×15 vs surgery → adjuvant pembrolizumab ×18 — 200 mg q3w, 18 total doses in both arms
endpoints: ⏳ Immature — 36 deaths in total (14 vs 22), too few for a definitive comparison
takeaway: Giving the same total amount of pembrolizumab but moving three doses in front of surgery improved 2-year event-free survival by over 20 percentage points. It is the proof of concept that neoadjuvant ICI beats purely adjuvant ICI — sequence, not dose or duration, is what changed. OS is still immature.

name: CheckMate-067
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III–IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 weeks earlier. Active brain metastases excluded. BRAF-mutant 31.5%.
treatment: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w vs nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w + placebo vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w ×4 + placebo
endpoints: ✅ 11.5 vs 6.9 vs 2.9 mo (combination vs nivolumab vs ipilimumab) — HR vs ipilimumab 0.42 (0.31–0.57) and 0.57 (0.43–0.76), both P<0.001; 3-yr PFS 39% vs 32% vs 10%
70.4% vs 54.1% vs 40.6% at 3 yr (CR+PR+SD; calculated — not reported as DCR in either paper)
takeaway: Nivolumab, with or without ipilimumab, beat ipilimumab alone in advanced melanoma on PFS, OS and ORR. The combination was significantly more toxic.

name: ARASENS
population: mHSPC; no prior treatment allowed. Visceral mets 17%.
treatment: Darolutamide 600 mg BID + ADT + docetaxel (triplet) vs placebo + ADT + docetaxel
takeaway: Adding darolutamide to ADT + docetaxel improved overall survival and the other secondary endpoints. Patients fit for docetaxel are candidates for first-line triplet therapy; the noted adverse-effect concern is cardiac disorders.

name: ARCHES
population: mHSPC. High-volume 63%. Prior therapy allowed: docetaxel 18%, ADT ≤3 mo 72%, >3 mo 20%. Gleason ≥8 67%.
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Enzalutamide plus ADT improved rPFS, OS and the other key secondary endpoints in mHSPC, with benefit regardless of disease burden and prior treatment. Watch for side effects: hypertension and CNS effects (fatigue, cognitive decline).

name: CHAARTED
population: Treatment-naive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; prior adjuvant ADT allowed if completed ≥12 mo earlier. Prespecified high-volume disease (visceral mets, or ≥4 bone mets with ≥1 non-axial) in ~65%; Gleason ≥8 ~60%; 75% de novo.
treatment: ADT + docetaxel 75 mg/m² q3w ×6 vs ADT alone
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to ADT improved OS and time to CRPC in high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. No benefit was observed in low-volume disease (OS HR 0.60, 0.32–1.13, P=0.11).

name: ENZAMET
population: mHSPC; high-volume 52%, Gleason ≥8 60%. Prior therapy allowed: 45% planned early docetaxel, 50% anti-androgen, 70% ADT.
treatment: Enzalutamide + ADT (± early docetaxel) vs standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen (bicalutamide/nilutamide/flutamide) + ADT (± early docetaxel)
takeaway: Enzalutamide + ADT improved clinical PFS, OS and other key secondary endpoints versus first-generation anti-androgens + ADT. The OS benefit was attenuated in the planned early-docetaxel subgroup.

name: CAPItello-281
population: PTEN-deficient de novo mHSPC. High-risk/high-volume disease 60%/74%. Prior abiraterone ~10%; no prior chemotherapy. Gleason ≥8 ~80%.
treatment: Capivasertib 400 mg BID (4 days on, 3 days off) + abiraterone + ADT vs placebo + abiraterone + ADT
takeaway: Capivasertib added to abiraterone + ADT improved rPFS and the other secondary endpoints in PTEN-deficient mHSPC. OS is still immature, and the combination causes hyperglycemia, diarrhea and rash.

name: GETUG-AFU 15
population: Metastatic, hormone-sensitive (non-castrate) prostate cancer, N=385 (192 vs 193); 67% (docetaxel arm) / 75% (ADT-alone arm) metastatic at initial diagnosis; median age 63–64; 81% bone mets.
treatment: ADT + docetaxel vs ADT alone
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to ADT did not improve OS in this trial (HR 1.01), in contrast to CHAARTED, despite improving all secondary endpoints (biochemical PFS, clinical PFS, PSA response). OS was confounded by crossover: 62% of the ADT-alone arm received docetaxel at castration resistance vs only 28% re-treated in the docetaxel arm. Median OS was longer than historical series in both arms (54–59 months), suggesting the trial may have been underpowered for the effect size assumed in its sample-size calculation.

name: LATITUDE
population: High-risk (≥2 of Gleason ≥8, ≥3 bone mets, visceral mets), treatment-naive mHSPC; prior therapy not allowed.
treatment: Abiraterone + prednisone + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Abiraterone + prednisone added to ADT improved rPFS and OS, plus the other key secondary endpoints, in high-risk treatment-naive mHSPC. The main watch-point is mineralocorticoid-excess side effects (hypertension, hypokalaemia).

name: PEACE-1
population: De novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). 60.6% received docetaxel; 43.1% low-volume (CHAARTED criteria).
treatment: 2×2 factorial: SOC (ADT ± docetaxel) ± abiraterone, ± prostate RT (74 Gy/37 fr)
endpoints: rPFS, low-volume, RT+AAP vs AAP alone (1°)
rPFS, low-volume, RT vs no RT (no AAP)
rPFS, ITT, AAP+RT vs abiraterone alone
OS (1°), ITT, pooled RT vs no RT
❌ HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.83–1.14), P=0.75 — no OS benefit from adding RT
takeaway: The only scenario in which adding RT improved rPFS was RT + abiraterone in low-volume disease, and adding RT delayed progression to CRPC. There was no OS benefit from adding RT overall.

name: INT-0162 (SWOG S9346)
population: Treatment-naive mHSPC; ECOG 0–2. Gleason ≥8 ~20%, visceral mets 6–7%, extensive disease ~50%.
treatment: Non-inferiority design: 7-mo ADT + bicalutamide, randomized if PSA ≤4 to continuous ADT vs intermittent ADT (resume ADT when PSA ≥20 or back to baseline; after 7 mo, stop ADT once PSA ≤4)
endpoints: ⚠️ Statistically inconclusive — HR 1.10 (0.99–1.23), boundary 1.2; cannot state intermittent ADT was significantly inferior to continuous ADT
takeaway: Intermittent ADT seemed non-inferior to continuous ADT, but the non-inferiority boundary was not statistically met, so inferiority could not be excluded or established. Continuous ADT remained standard of care.

name: HERO
population: ⚠️ Mixed population: 31.7% metastatic (22.7% de novo), 50.2% relapsed non-metastatic, 27.1% locally advanced.
treatment: Relugolix (oral GnRH antagonist) vs leuprolide
endpoints: ✅ 96.7% vs 88.8% through 48 wk (testosterone <50 ng/dL) — +7.9%, P<0.001 for superiority
Not assessed (trial did not assess PFS or OS)
takeaway: Oral relugolix achieved a higher sustained castration rate than leuprolide and a lower rate of MACE (54% lower). The trial did not assess oncologic efficacy and enrolled a mixed-stage population, so it is not specific to metastatic disease.

name: HERO
population: ⚠️ Cross-listed from the Metastatic database: the population spans several disease settings. N=930 (622 vs 308); 50.2% had biochemical/clinical relapse after curative local therapy (non-metastatic), 27.1% advanced localized disease unsuitable for curative local intervention, 31.7% metastatic (22.7% newly diagnosed androgen-sensitive). Pharmacodynamic/cardiovascular endpoints rather than DFS/OS/pCR.
treatment: Relugolix (oral GnRH antagonist) vs leuprolide (injectable LHRH agonist), both as androgen-deprivation therapy
endpoints: ✅ 96.7% vs 88.8% (testosterone <50 ng/dL through 48 wk) — diff 7.9 pts (95% CI 4.1–11.8), P<0.001 for superiority
Castrate by day 4 with relugolix vs a surge to ~625 ng/dL with leuprolide
takeaway: Oral relugolix gave rapid, sustained testosterone suppression that was statistically superior to injectable leuprolide, with no testosterone surge. It carried a 54% lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, most pronounced in patients with pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors (>90% of the trial). Same trial as the Metastatic database entry, cross-listed because the population is mostly non-metastatic; it is not a curative-intent treatment-intensification trial.

name: STAMPEDE (Docetaxel, Arm C)
population: Treatment-naive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; 76% assessable by the CHAARTED definition (44% low-burden, 56% high-burden). ~70% Gleason ≥8; ~95% de novo.
treatment: SOC (ADT) + docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV Q3W ×6 + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs SOC (ADT) alone (2:1)
endpoints: ✅ Low-burden 93.2 vs 76.7 mo; high-burden 39.9 vs 35.2 mo — ↔ no heterogeneity by metastatic burden (interaction P=0.827)
takeaway: Docetaxel + ADT improved OS in metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer regardless of metastatic burden, in contrast to the CHAARTED subgroup pattern. STAMPEDE's low-burden subgroup was larger (n=362), and FFS, PFS, mPFS and PCSS were also improved.

name: STAMPEDE (Abiraterone, Arm G) — M1
population: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer from STAMPEDE Arm G (75% M1, 25% M0). Gleason ≥8 in 75%.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg QD + prednisolone 5 mg QD + ADT vs ADT alone
endpoints: ↔ None for OS (interaction P=0.37) or FFS (P=0.08)
takeaway: Adding abiraterone to ADT improved FFS and OS in this hormone-sensitive cohort. The headline figures are trial-wide (M1 + M0), with no heterogeneity of effect by metastatic status.

name: STAMPEDE (Abiraterone, Arm G) — M0
population: Pre-specified non-metastatic (M0) subgroup of STAMPEDE's abiraterone comparison (n=915 of 1917: 455 SOC / 460 SOC+abiraterone). Newly diagnosed node-positive M0, or node-negative M0 high-risk locally advanced (≥2 of T3/T4, Gleason 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL), starting long-term ADT; or relapsing after radical local therapy with high-risk features. Reported RT use ~39–40% in both arms. Companion entry: STAMPEDE (Abiraterone, Arm G) — M1 (Metastatic DB).
treatment: SOC (ADT) + abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg once daily vs SOC (ADT) alone; RT mandated (node-negative) or encouraged (node-positive)
endpoints: ⏳ Deaths 34/460 (7%) vs 44/455 (10%) — HR 0.75 (0.48–1.18), immature (78 deaths in M0 at data freeze)
↔ No heterogeneity of effect (interaction P=0.37 OS, P=0.08 FFS)
takeaway: Adding abiraterone to ADT improved failure-free survival in the non-metastatic subgroup (HR 0.21), even though abiraterone was capped at 2 years here. The OS signal (HR 0.75, 0.48–1.18) is directionally favourable but immature, with only 78 deaths. There was no heterogeneity versus the metastatic subgroup, supporting benefit across the disease spectrum, at the cost of more grade 3–5 AEs.

name: TITAN
population: mHSPC. High-volume 63%. Prior docetaxel allowed (11%). Gleason ≥8 67%.
treatment: Apalutamide 240 mg/day + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Apalutamide plus ADT improved rPFS, OS and the other key secondary endpoints, with benefit regardless of disease burden and prior treatment. Watch for side effects: rash, hypothyroidism and ischemic heart disease.

name: ARTEMIS-008
population: SCLC after 1L chemotherapy. Stable brain mets 20%, prior ICI 80%, chemo-free interval <90 d ~36%.
treatment: Risvutatug rezetecan 8 mg/kg Q3W vs topotecan 1.2 mg/m² D1–5 Q3W
takeaway: Risvutatug rezetecan improved PFS and OS over topotecan in 2L SCLC and is the first B7-H3 ADC with an OS benefit. Notable side effects are ILD and haematologic toxicity.

name: AFFIRM
population: mCRPC after docetaxel. ECOG 2 in 9%; visceral (liver/lung) metastases 23%.
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d vs placebo
takeaway: Enzalutamide improved both rPFS and OS versus placebo in mCRPC after docetaxel. Adverse effects to watch are fatigue and seizure.

name: COU-AA-301
population: mCRPC after docetaxel. ECOG 2 in 10%. Bone mets ~89%, liver 10%. Median PSA ~130.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs placebo + prednisolone
takeaway: Abiraterone plus prednisolone improved rPFS and OS over placebo plus prednisolone in mCRPC after docetaxel. Mineralocorticoid-related side effects are the toxicity to watch.

name: COU-AA-302
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC with no visceral metastases.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs placebo + prednisolone
takeaway: Abiraterone + prednisolone improved rPFS and OS versus placebo in pre-docetaxel mCRPC. Visceral metastases were excluded, and the OS HR crossed the efficacy boundary only at the 4th interim analysis.

name: PREVAIL
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC. Visceral metastases allowed (~12%).
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d vs placebo
takeaway: Enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS versus placebo in mCRPC before docetaxel. The population included visceral metastases (~12%).

name: MAGNITUDE
population: 1L mCRPC with an HRR alteration required. Prior ARPI for nmCRPC/mCSPC, or abiraterone + prednisone for up to 4 months in mCRPC, was allowed. BRCA1/2 subgroup 53%.
treatment: Niraparib 200 mg QD + abiraterone/prednisone (AAP) vs placebo + AAP
takeaway: Niraparib + AAP improved rPFS but not OS versus AAP in 1L HRR+ mCRPC. The benefit is concentrated in the BRCA subgroup; other secondary endpoints were positive.

name: PROfound
population: mCRPC with progression on enzalutamide or abiraterone; HRR mutation required. Cohort A: ≥1 mutation in BRCA1, BRCA2 or ATM; Cohort B: ≥1 mutation in 12 HRR genes. Visceral 27%/35%. Prior taxane 65%, prior abiraterone 40%, prior enzalutamide 40%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs investigator's-choice ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide)
takeaway: Olaparib monotherapy improved rPFS and OS over an ARPI in BRCA/ATM-mutant mCRPC after prior ARPI. Caveat: crossover was 81%.

name: PROpel
population: 1L mCRPC irrespective of HRR status. HRR-mutated ~28%; BRCA1 2%/1%, BRCA2 10%/9%. Visceral disease ~12%; prior docetaxel ~22%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID + abiraterone/prednisone (AAP) vs placebo + AAP
endpoints: ⏳ NR vs NR (28.6% maturity) — HR 0.86 (0.66–1.12), P=0.29, immature
takeaway: Olaparib + abiraterone improved ibPFS and PFS2 versus abiraterone in 1L mCRPC regardless of HRR status, but OS is immature. The benefit is concentrated in HRR-mutated disease (HR 0.50 vs 0.76); watch for anemia and VTE.

name: TALAPRO-2
population: 1L mCRPC irrespective of HRR status. HRR-mutant 21%, BRCA1/2 7%. Visceral 14%; prior taxane 22%.
treatment: Talazoparib + enzalutamide vs. placebo + enzalutamide
endpoints: ✅ HRR+ 27.9 vs 16.4 mo; ⚠️ HRR− NR vs 22.5 mo
takeaway: Talazoparib + enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS versus enzalutamide alone in first-line mCRPC unselected for HRR status. The benefit is greater in HRR-mutant patients (OS HR 0.55), and OS was not significantly improved in HRR-negative patients (HR 0.88). Significant haematologic adverse events occur, reportedly more than with olaparib or niraparib.

name: TRITON2
population: mCRPC with a BRCA mutation (n=115), progressed after ARPI and taxane (median 2 prior CRPC therapies). BRCA1 n=13, BRCA2 n=71; germline n=44. Prior abiraterone 64.3%, enzalutamide 71.3%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID (single-arm, phase 2)
takeaway: Rucaparib monotherapy achieved an ORR of 43.5% in heavily pretreated BRCA1/2-mutant mCRPC. This is a single-arm phase 2 study with no comparator, and OS is immature (1-yr OS 73.0%).

name: ALSYMPCA
population: Symptomatic mCRPC with ≥2 bone metastases and no visceral metastases; median age 71, ECOG 0–2. 57% had received prior docetaxel (or were ineligible for/declined it) and 57% had WHO pain-ladder score ≥2 requiring regular analgesics or recent EBRT.
treatment: Radium-223 vs placebo, both + best standard of care (BSC) — Ra-223 50 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6
takeaway: Radium-223 improved OS and time to first symptomatic skeletal event versus placebo plus best standard of care in symptomatic mCRPC with bone metastases. It was the first OS benefit shown for a bone-targeted radiopharmaceutical.

name: ERA-223
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC with bone metastases; no visceral metastases; prior ARPi excluded.
treatment: Radium-223 + AAP vs placebo + AAP (Ra-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6; AA 1000 mg/d + prednisone 5 mg BID)
takeaway: Adding radium-223 to AAP did not improve SSE-free survival, and OS was numerically lower. Fracture risk was higher than with AAP alone, and the combination is now contraindicated with AAP.

name: PEACE-3
population: First-line mCRPC with bone mets; no visceral mets. 30% prior docetaxel.
treatment: Radium-223 + enzalutamide vs enzalutamide alone (open-label); enzalutamide 160 mg/d, Ra-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6; bone-protecting agent mandatory
endpoints: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event
takeaway: Adding radium-223 to enzalutamide improved radiographic PFS and OS versus enzalutamide alone in first-line mCRPC with bone metastases. A bone-protecting agent was mandatory, and the combination carries increased fracture and ONJ risk versus enzalutamide alone.

name: CARD
population: mCRPC with prior docetaxel (≥3 cycles) AND prior ARSI (abiraterone or enzalutamide) with PD <12 mo. Prior ARPI: abiraterone 43%, enzalutamide 56%. Gleason ≥8 ~60%.
treatment: Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² IV q3w vs alternative ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide)
takeaway: Cabazitaxel improved imaging-based PFS and OS versus an alternative ARPI in mCRPC after docetaxel and a first ARPI. The trial confirms the poor efficacy of an ARPI switch after early progression.

name: VISION
population: mCRPC after ≥1 ARPI and 1–2 taxane regimens (38% prior cabazitaxel; 40% two prior ARPIs). Visceral metastases ~20%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 + standard of care vs standard of care alone (2:1; SOC excludes chemotherapy, other radioligand therapy, immunotherapy)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 plus standard of care improved rPFS and OS versus standard of care alone in post-taxane, post-ARPI, PSMA-PET-selected mCRPC. The trial led to FDA approval.

name: TheraP
population: mCRPC after docetaxel. Visceral disease 7%; 90% prior ARPI.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 vs cabazitaxel (open-label); crossover 32%/20%
endpoints: ✅ 5.1 vs 5.1 mo — HR 0.63 (0.46–0.86), P=0.0028; 1-yr PFS 19% vs 3%, benefit emerges after 6 mo
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved PSA response and PFS over cabazitaxel in post-docetaxel mCRPC, but OS did not differ. Caveats: OS is confounded by crossover, and side effects include thrombocytopenia and dry mouth.

name: PSMAfore
population: mCRPC, taxane-naive, with PD on one ARPI (abiraterone, enzalutamide, darolutamide or apalutamide). Visceral disease 13%; 81% had the prior ARPI in the CRPC setting.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 vs switch ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide); 57% crossover
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved rPFS and time to SSE versus switching to a second ARPI in taxane-naive mCRPC. There was no OS difference (HR 0.98), and OS is confounded by the 57% crossover.

name: TAX 327
population: mCRPC (PD on ADT), chemotherapy-naive; ~90% bone mets.
treatment: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² q3w (D3P) vs docetaxel 30 mg/m² weekly (D1P) vs mitoxantrone q3w (MP), all + prednisolone 5 mg BID
takeaway: Docetaxel q3w + prednisone improved OS, pain, PSA response and quality of life versus mitoxantrone in mCRPC. Weekly docetaxel did not improve OS, so D3P became the standard of care.

name: BILCAP
population: Resected biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder cancer), R0/R1, ECOG <2 (ECOG 1 ~50%). Stage I–III: II 60%, III 13%/8%.
treatment: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID D1–14 q3w for 24 wk vs observation
takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine showed an overall survival benefit in the per-protocol and adjusted sensitivity analyses and is standard of care. However, the primary ITT overall survival analysis was not significant (P=0.097), and the recurrence-free survival benefit was seen only while patients were on capecitabine, with recurrences after 24 weeks.

name: FUGA-BT (JCOG1113)
population: Chemotherapy-naive advanced/recurrent biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder/ampullary cancer), ECOG PS 0-1, enrolled across 33 institutions in Japan. Primary tumor sites were roughly balanced (gallbladder ~39%, intrahepatic ~27%, extrahepatic ~30%, ampulla ~3-4%) and about 60% had metastatic disease.
treatment: Gemcitabine + S-1 (GS) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC)
endpoints: ↔ 15.1 vs 13.4 mo (median) — HR 0.945 (90% CI 0.777-1.149), P=0.046 for non-inferiority
takeaway: Gemcitabine + S-1 is non-inferior to gemcitabine–cisplatin as first-line therapy for biliary tract cancer — a non-inferiority result, not a superiority win. It caused less haematologic toxicity but more mucosal adverse events, and the trial was run in Japan.

name: KHBO1401-MITSUBA
population: Advanced biliary tract cancer (unresectable or recurrent adenocarcinoma/adenosquamous carcinoma of the bile duct, gallbladder, or ampulla), ECOG PS 0-2, across 39 centers in Japan (Kansai Hepatobiliary Oncology Group). About three-quarters of patients had unresectable disease and one-quarter had recurrence after surgery.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin + S-1 (GCS) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC)
takeaway: Adding S-1 to gemcitabine–cisplatin improved PFS, OS and ORR versus gemcitabine–cisplatin in first-line advanced biliary tract cancer. The OS gain was modest (13.5 vs 12.6 months), and the trial was run in Japan.

name: TOPAZ-1
population: Treatment-naive advanced biliary tract cancer, ECOG PS 0–1, global. ECOG 0 ~50%, iCCA ~55%, metastatic ~90%, PD-L1-positive ~60%.
treatment: Durvalumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + gemcitabine/cisplatin; no maintenance gemcitabine
takeaway: Adding durvalumab to gemcitabine/cisplatin improved OS, PFS and ORR in 1L advanced BTC and is the standard of care.

name: KEYNOTE-966
population: Treatment-naive advanced BTC, ECOG PS 0–1, global enrolment. ECOG 0 in 43–48%; iCCA 60%; metastatic ~90%; PD-L1 positive ~70%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + gemcitabine/cisplatin; maintenance gemcitabine-pembrolizumab
takeaway: Adding pembrolizumab to gemcitabine/cisplatin improved OS in 1L advanced BTC. PFS did not clear its significance threshold (P=0.023 > 0.0125) and ORR was identical (29% vs 29%).

name: ABC-02
population: Advanced biliary tract cancer, PS 0–2 (ECOG 2 ~10%), conducted in the UK. Metastatic disease ~75%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC) vs gemcitabine alone, up to 8 cycles (24 wk)
takeaway: ABC-02 established gemcitabine + cisplatin as the standard of care in first-line advanced biliary tract cancer. Compared with gemcitabine alone it improved both OS (HR 0.64) and PFS (HR 0.63).

name: ABC-06
population: Advanced biliary tract cancer with progression on 1L gemcitabine-cisplatin. ECOG 0–1. UK.
treatment: FOLFOX (up to 12 cycles) + active symptom control (ASC) vs ASC alone
endpoints: 4.0 mo (FOLFOX arm only; no routine imaging in ASC-alone arm)
takeaway: FOLFOX plus active symptom control improved OS over ASC alone in 2L advanced BTC and is the 2L standard of care. Caveat: the benefit is driven by the 6- and 12-month OS tail.

name: ClarIDHy
population: Cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior treatment and an IDH1 mutation.
treatment: Ivosidenib vs placebo (2:1); crossover 57%
takeaway: Ivosidenib improved PFS over placebo in previously treated IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma. ITT OS was not significant because of 57% crossover, while the RPSFT-adjusted analysis showed an OS benefit.

name: HERIZON-GEA-01
population: Previously untreated, HER2-positive (IHC3+ or IHC2+/ISH+) unresectable locally advanced/recurrent/metastatic gastric, GEJ, or esophageal adenocarcinoma.
treatment: Zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemo vs zanidatamab + chemo vs trastuzumab + chemo (1:1:1)
takeaway: Zanidatamab (a biparatopic HER2 bispecific antibody) + chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab (anti-PD-1), improved PFS over trastuzumab + chemotherapy in first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, beating the 15-year-old trastuzumab standard. The triplet with tislelizumab also improved OS at the first interim, whereas OS with zanidatamab + chemo was not yet significant (further analyses planned). Diarrhea is the dominant adverse event with zanidatamab-based regimens.

name: KEYNOTE-158
population: MSI-H/dMMR non-CRC solid tumors with progression on at least 1 prior therapy; cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) n=22 (9.4%).
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy (single-arm)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab produced an ORR of 34.3% across previously treated MSI-H/dMMR non-CRC solid tumors (40.9% in CCA), with OS better than a historical chemotherapy control. It underpins the tumor-agnostic FDA approval for dMMR/MSI-H cancers; this is a single-arm trial.

name: NIFTY
population: Metastatic biliary tract cancer with progression on 1L gemcitabine-cisplatin. ECOG 0–1. South Korea.
treatment: Liposomal irinotecan + 5-FU/LV vs 5-FU/LV alone (chemotherapy indefinite)
takeaway: Liposomal irinotecan plus 5-FU/LV improved PFS and OS over 5-FU/LV alone in 2L metastatic BTC. The ORR difference did not reach significance (P=0.068).

name: VISION
population: Metastatic NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping mutation (liquid and/or tissue biopsy); ≤2 prior lines; ECOG 0–1. Stable/treated brain metastases 11%.
treatment: Tepotinib monotherapy (single-arm)
endpoints: 8.5 mo total; 8.5 mo liquid; 11.0 mo tissue
takeaway: Tepotinib produced an ORR of 46% in NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping, with similar rates by liquid (48%) and tissue (50%) biopsy. This was a single-arm trial with immature OS, and peripheral edema was the notable class adverse event.

name: LUMINOSITY
population: Advanced/metastatic c-Met protein-overexpressing (IHC ≥25% 3+), nonsquamous EGFR-wildtype NSCLC; ≤2 prior lines (≤1 prior cytotoxic chemotherapy); ECOG 0–1. 98% prior platinum, 82% prior ICI.
treatment: Telisotuzumab vedotin (Teliso-V) monotherapy, single-arm
endpoints: 5.7 mo (4.6–6.9) total; 5.5 (4.1–8.3) c-Met high; 6.0 (4.5–8.1) c-Met intermediate
14.5 mo (9.9–16.6) total; 14.6 c-Met high; 14.2 c-Met intermediate
takeaway: Telisotuzumab vedotin (c-Met-directed ADC, MMAE payload) monotherapy gave an ORR of 28.6% (34.6% in c-Met high) in a heavily pretreated, c-Met protein-overexpressing nonsquamous EGFR-WT NSCLC population. Selection is by protein expression (IHC), distinct from MET exon 14/amplification-driven approaches, giving a larger (~25%) eligible population. Squamous and EGFR-mutant cohorts closed for futility; the results support an ongoing phase 3 vs docetaxel.

name: FIGHT-202
population: Cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior therapy and FGFR2 fusion. Other FGFR2 alterations enrolled as a comparator cohort.
treatment: Pemigatinib monotherapy (single-arm); pan-FGFR1–3 TKI
endpoints: ✅ FGFR2 fusion 35.5% vs 0% in both other cohorts
FGFR2 fusion 6.9 vs 2.1 (other FGF/FGFR) vs 1.7 (no) mo
FGFR2 fusion 21.1 vs 6.7 (other FGF/FGFR) vs 4.0 (no) mo
takeaway: Pemigatinib gave an ORR of 35.5% in second-line or later FGFR2 fusion cholangiocarcinoma, with PFS and OS better than a historical chemotherapy control. Patients with other FGF/FGFR alterations had 0% ORR, and hyperphosphatemia is a class adverse effect.

name: FOENIX-CCA2
population: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion and ≥1 prior treatment; 57% had ≥2 prior treatments.
treatment: Futibatinib (irreversible pan-FGFR1–4 TKI) monotherapy, single-arm
takeaway: Futibatinib produced an ORR of 42% by BICR in previously treated FGFR2-fusion intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. This is a single-arm trial, so the PFS and OS figures have no comparator.

name: ROAR
population: Previously treated BRAF V600E advanced rare cancers, no prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor. N=206.
treatment: Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg QD (single-arm basket, no control)
endpoints: ✅ ATC 56%, BTC 53%, LGG 54%, HGG 33%, ASI 67% (2/3), HCL 89%, MM 50%, GIST 0% (1 pt, SD)
ATC 6.7, BTC 9.0, HGG 5.5, ASI 9.5, MM 6.3; LGG, HCL: NE
ATC 14.5, BTC 13.5, HGG 17.6, ASI 21.8, MM 33.9; LGG, HCL: NE
ATC 14.4, BTC 8.9, HGG 31.2, MM 11.1, ASI 7.7; LGG/HCL NR
takeaway: Dabrafenib + trametinib gave an ORR of about 50% in 2L BRAF V600E-mutant rare cancers. This supported an FDA tumour-agnostic approval for BRAF V600E-mutant cancers, with CRC expected to be excluded. The trial is single-arm with no control.

name: PSMAddition
population: PSMA-PET-positive mHSPC (PSMA-negative lesions not an exclusion). Treatment-naive or ≤45 days of ARPI/ADT (90%). High-volume 68%, de novo 50%, visceral (lung/liver) 15%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 7.4 GBq ±10% ×6 + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI (1:1, open-label); crossover 16%
endpoints: ✅ NR vs NR (interim; events 24% vs 30%) — HR 0.72 (0.58–0.90), P=0.0021
⏳ NR vs NR (interim, immature) — HR 0.84 (0.63–1.13), P=0.13
⚠️ More AEs (dry mouth, cytopenias, GI); HRQoL time-to-worsening HR ~1.1
takeaway: First phase 3 radioligand trial in mHSPC: adding ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 to ADT + ARPI improved rPFS (HR 0.72). OS is immature and not significant (HR 0.84), with 16% crossover; adverse events were more frequent (dry mouth, cytopenias, GI) and HRQoL time-to-worsening HR was ~1.1.

name: IMvigor010
population: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (bladder 93%, UTUC 7%) after radical surgery + LND: ypT2–4a/ypN+ post-NAC, or pT3–4a/pN+ without NAC (cisplatin-ineligible/declined). pN+ 52%; prior NAC 48%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W × 1 yr vs observation
takeaway: This first phase 3 adjuvant ICI trial in MIUC was negative for DFS and OS, with no benefit by PD-L1. In the exploratory analysis, ctDNA+ patients (37%) had an OS benefit with atezolizumab (HR 0.59) while ctDNA− patients had no benefit and more AEs, a hypothesis prospectively tested in IMvigor011.

name: LAURA
population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC (AJCC 8th) with EGFR Ex19del or L858R and no progression after platinum chemoradiotherapy. Asian 82%.
treatment: Osimertinib 80 mg QD vs placebo (2:1) until progression; crossover allowed
takeaway: Osimertinib after chemoradiotherapy markedly improved PFS in EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III NSCLC, so EGFR should be tested before chemoRT. OS is immature (20% maturity) and confounded by high crossover (81%).

name: ARIEL3
population: High-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer (HGSC/EC) with CA-125 <ULN, enrolled regardless of HRD/BRCA status. BRCAm 35%, HRD 63%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs placebo (2:1)
endpoints: BRCAm 38% vs 9%; HRD 27% vs 7%; ITT 18% vs 8%
takeaway: Rucaparib improved PFS in 2L platinum-sensitive disease regardless of BRCA/HRD status, with the 1° PFS tested hierarchically BRCAm → HRD → ITT. There was no OS benefit.

name: AtTEnd
population: Newly diagnosed residual/inoperable stage III–IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (no prior chemo for recurrence; prior adjuvant platinum OK if PFI ≥6 mo); carcinosarcoma allowed; ECOG 0–2. Recurrent 67%, Asian 20%, central dMMR 23%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1200 mg + CP q3w × 6–8 → atezolizumab q3w until PD vs placebo + CP → placebo (2:1)
endpoints: ⚠️ 38.7 vs 30.2 mo (interim, not significant) — HR 0.82 (0.63–1.07), P=0.048 vs boundary 0.024; dMMR NE vs 25.7 mo, HR 0.41 (0.22–0.76)
↔ No difference by MMR or PD-L1 status (data in appendix)
takeaway: Atezolizumab + chemo followed by atezolizumab improved PFS in 1L endometrial cancer, driven by dMMR (HR 0.36) with an overall HR of 0.74. There was no benefit in pMMR (PFS HR 0.92, OS HR 1.00), unlike RUBY, GY018 and DUO-E, and OS is interim and not significant.

name: LIBRETTO-431
population: Treatment-naive advanced/metastatic non-squamous RET fusion-positive NSCLC; brain mets 22%; optional crossover at PD.
treatment: Selpercatinib (n=159) vs platinum + pemetrexed ± pembrolizumab (n=102)
endpoints: ORR 82% vs 58%; ✅ CNS progression cause-specific HR 0.28 (0.12–0.68), 12-mo 6% vs 20%
takeaway: First-line selpercatinib improved PFS (24.8 vs 11.2 mo) over chemo ± pembrolizumab and establishes the 1L standard in RET fusion-positive NSCLC. It clearly reduced CNS progression (12-mo 6% vs 20%); monitor LFTs and hypertension, and OS is immature.

name: NETTER-1
population: Grade 1–2, SSTR-positive midgut NET with progression on standard octreotide LAR. Ileum 74%, liver mets 83%, G1 69%.
treatment: 177Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV q8w × 4 + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg q4w
takeaway: 177Lu-Dotatate improved PFS and ORR in SSA-refractory midgut NET and is standard of care. The OS difference was not significant, with 36% crossover, and adverse effects include cytopenia and MDS.

name: PRIMA
population: High-risk FIGO stage III–IV HGSC/EC, fallopian or peritoneal cancer, regardless of HRD status; prior bevacizumab allowed. CR 70%, stage III 65%, HRD 51%, NACT 67%.
treatment: Niraparib 300 mg QD vs placebo (2:1), up to 3 years; niraparib dose adjusted by body weight and platelets
takeaway: Niraparib maintenance after 1L platinum-taxane chemotherapy in high-risk ovarian cancer improved PFS regardless of HRD status, but not OS. Grade ≥3 haematologic adverse events were high.

name: RADIANT-4
population: Grade 1–2 non-functional GI/lung NET: lung 30%, GI 58%, unknown primary 12%. Prior SSA >50%; prior chemo ~25%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily vs placebo (2:1), both with best supportive care
endpoints: ⏳ Immature (interim; NR) — HR 0.64 (0.40–1.05), P=0.037 vs boundary 0.0002
