takeaway: Everolimus improved PFS in non-functional GI/lung NET and is standard of care as 2L. OS showed a trend that was not significant at the first interim analysis (P=0.037 vs boundary 0.0002).

name: SOLO-2
population: HGSC/EC with germline BRCA mutation.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs placebo (2:1)
takeaway: Olaparib improved PFS in germline BRCA-mutant disease. OS was not significant but becomes significant when adjusted for crossover (38%); MDS/AML occurred in 8% with long exposure.

name: IMvigor011
population: Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after cystectomy, (y)pT2–4aN0 or (y)pT0–4aN+, no radiologic disease, ECOG 0–2. 761 were enrolled in ctDNA surveillance (q6w ×9 mo + 1 yr) and 250 ctDNA-positive patients were randomized; among them N+ 57% and T3/T4 72%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1680 mg Q4W ×1 yr vs placebo (2:1), only if ctDNA+ on serial monitoring
takeaway: This is the first prospective ctDNA-guided adjuvant randomized trial, and it showed both DFS and OS benefit with atezolizumab in ctDNA-positive patients. Patients with persistent ctDNA negativity had a 2-year DFS of 88% without treatment, which supports de-escalation. The OS benefit was seen regardless of PD-L1, but follow-up is short (16.1 months).

name: LIBRETTO-432
population: Stage IB–IIIA RET fusion-positive NSCLC after definitive therapy (surgery or RT ± adjuvant chemotherapy). Primary analysis in stage II–IIIA (n=109). East Asia ≈57%; prior systemic therapy ≈91%.
treatment: Selpercatinib up to 3 yr (n=75) vs placebo (n=76)
takeaway: This is the first adjuvant targeted therapy in RET fusion-positive NSCLC, with a large EFS benefit (HR 0.17). OS is immature, EFS is not the same as cure, and elevated liver function tests are common.

name: ARROW
population: Advanced/metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC, treatment-naive or post-platinum. Efficacy population N=281; history of brain metastases 35%; KIF5B 70%.
treatment: Pralsetinib 400 mg QD (single-arm)
takeaway: In this single-arm trial, pralsetinib gave an ORR of 70%, mDoR of 19.1 mo and mOS of 44.3 mo at the final analysis, leading to FDA approval in 2020 (accelerated) and 2023 (regular). Toxicity includes cytopenia, pneumonitis and infection, and KIF5B-RET carries a worse prognosis.

name: DUO-E
population: Newly diagnosed measurable stage III / stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (1L; prior adjuvant chemotherapy allowed if relapse ≥12 mo). Carcinosarcoma allowed. pMMR 80%, recurrent 52%, PD-L1+ (TAP ≥1%) ~67%.
treatment: CP + durvalumab → durvalumab + olaparib vs CP + durvalumab → durvalumab vs CP + placebo (3 arms, 1:1:1)
endpoints: ✅ D+O 15.1 vs D 10.2 vs control 9.6 mo — D+O vs control HR 0.55 (0.43–0.69), P<0.0001; D vs control HR 0.71 (0.57–0.89), P=0.003
⚠️ NR vs NR vs 25.9 mo (IA1, 28% maturity) — D+O HR 0.59 (0.42–0.83), P=0.003; D HR 0.77 (0.56–1.07), P=0.12 (interim, not significant)
takeaway: Adding durvalumab to CP then maintenance durvalumab, with or without olaparib, improved PFS in both arms in first-line endometrial cancer. Olaparib adds benefit mainly in pMMR (HR 0.76 vs durvalumab) and PD-L1+ patients, with none in dMMR (HR 0.97), and there was little benefit in the PD-L1− subgroup. OS is immature.

name: KEYNOTE-775
population: Advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer after 1 prior platinum (2 allowed if one was (neo)adjuvant); no prior ICI or VEGF-targeted therapy; any histology except carcinosarcoma/sarcoma; ECOG 0–1. pMMR 84%; serous 26%.
treatment: Lenvatinib 20 mg QD + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (≤35 doses) vs treatment of physician's choice: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² q3w or weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² (3 on / 1 off)
takeaway: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab after platinum improved PFS, OS and ORR versus doxorubicin or paclitaxel in advanced endometrial cancer, including in pMMR (OS HR 0.68). It is toxic, with grade ≥3 adverse events in 89%, lenvatinib dose reduction in two thirds, and hypothyroidism in 57%.

name: LIBRETTO-531
population: Kinase inhibitor-naive advanced/metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer. Optional crossover at progression.
treatment: Selpercatinib (n=193) vs cabozantinib or vandetanib (n=98)
takeaway: Selpercatinib beat cabozantinib or vandetanib on PFS (HR 0.28) and ORR in first-line RET-mutant MTC, leading to FDA regular approval, and it is better tolerated. OS was not reached in either arm, and crossover at progression was optional.

name: NETTER-2
population: Treatment-naive grade 2–3 SSTR-positive GEP-NET. Pancreas 54%, small intestine 29%; G3 35%; liver mets 90%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV q8w ×4 + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg q4w (2:1)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate improved PFS and ORR in first-line higher-grade GEP-NET. The ORR of 43% (CR 5%) is unusually high for a NET, and OS is immature.

name: PROMID
population: Treatment-naive, grade 1–2 midgut NET. Ki-67 ≤2% in 95%; functional 39%; SSA scan positive 75%; hepatic tumor burden ≤10% in ~75%.
treatment: Octreotide LAR 30 mg IM q28d vs placebo, until PFS event
takeaway: Octreotide LAR prolonged time to progression in first-line functional and non-functional midgut NET and is standard of care. As the very first SSA trial, it showed the drug works in both settings, so it is anti-proliferative and not only for symptom control; OS showed no difference (HR 0.81, P=0.77) with 76.7% crossover.

name: CLARINET
population: GEP-NET G1–2 (Ki-67 <10%), non-functioning, SSTR+. Pancreas 45%, midgut 36%; G1 ~70%. 96% stable disease at baseline; 84% treatment-naive.
treatment: Lanreotide 120 mg SC q28d vs placebo, up to 96 wk (24 doses)
takeaway: Lanreotide improved PFS over placebo in SSTR+ non-functioning G1–2 GEP-NET, even though 96% had stable disease at baseline, supporting starting an SSA early. OS showed no difference, with 46% crossover.

name: KEYNOTE-868 (NRG-GY018)
population: Measurable stage III/IVA, or stage IVB / recurrent endometrial cancer (± measurable disease); prior adjuvant chemotherapy allowed if ≥12 mo earlier; carcinosarcoma excluded; ECOG 0–2. Separate dMMR (n=225) and pMMR (n=591) cohorts.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin/paclitaxel ×6 → pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (≤14 cycles) vs placebo + carboplatin/paclitaxel → placebo
takeaway: Pembrolizumab with chemotherapy followed by pembrolizumab maintenance improved PFS in 1L advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer in both cohorts (dMMR HR 0.30, pMMR HR 0.54), with no excess chemotherapy toxicity and irAEs as expected. Caveat: OS is immature and pMMR median follow-up is only 7.9 mo.

name: CABINET
population: Grade 1–3 NET with progression on ≥1 prior therapy (besides SSA) within 1 yr. Extrapancreatic NET (epNET) n=203 (GI 57%, lung 19%); pancreatic NET (pNET) n=95. ~60% had prior Lu-177.
treatment: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily vs placebo (2:1), in two cohorts (epNET and pNET); crossover allowed
takeaway: Cabozantinib improved PFS and ORR in both pNET and epNET after Lu-177/everolimus, but OS did not differ. OS is immature because the trial stopped after the first interim analysis, and dose reduction was needed in 60% of patients.

name: ECOG-ACRIN E2211
population: Advanced/unresectable pancreatic NET, low/intermediate grade, radiographic progression within 12 mo. No prior temozolomide, DTIC, capecitabine or 5-FU; prior SSA 63%, everolimus ~35%, sunitinib ~10%. Liver metastases 94%.
treatment: CAPTEM (capecitabine 750 mg/m² BID D1–14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² D10–14, q28d) vs temozolomide alone (200 mg/m² D1–5, q28d), up to 13 cycles
takeaway: This is the only randomized trial of CAPTEM in pNET: adding capecitabine lengthens PFS (22.7 vs 14.4 mo, HR 0.58), with the highest ORR (~40%) of any randomized pNET regimen. The ~5-month OS gain is not significant and toxicity doubles (Gr3–4 45% vs 22%). MGMT deficiency predicts response (IHC-low ORR 52% vs 15%), so test it when tumour shrinkage is the goal.

name: KRYSTAL-10
population: KRAS G12C mCRC that progressed on 1L fluoropyrimidine-based oxaliplatin or irinotecan chemotherapy.
treatment: Adagrasib + cetuximab vs FOLFIRI or mFOLFOX ± anti-VEGF/VEGFR
takeaway: Adagrasib + cetuximab failed to improve PFS or OS versus 2L chemotherapy despite a higher ORR (47% vs 16%), and the FDA CRC indication was withdrawn.

name: NOVA (ENGOT-OV16)
population: Predominantly HGSC. Two cohorts: gBRCA (n=203) and non-gBRCA (n=350), the latter tested for HRD (myChoice).
treatment: Niraparib 300 mg QD vs placebo (2:1)
takeaway: Niraparib improved PFS in 2L gBRCA (HR 0.27) and non-gBRCA (HR 0.45) patients, but gave no OS benefit. Grade ≥3 thrombocytopenia occurred in 34%.

name: SUN1111
population: Grade 1–2 pancreatic NET with progression within 1 yr. Prior chemo 69%, prior SSA 36%; non-functioning ~50%. No prior TKI/VEGF inhibitor.
treatment: Sunitinib 37.5 mg PO daily (continuous) vs placebo, both with BSC (SSA allowed)
takeaway: Sunitinib improved PFS and ORR in progressive pancreatic NET, with OS immature. The trial stopped early because of toxicity in the placebo arm, and the benefit applies to pancreatic NET only, not GI NET.

name: EMERALD-1
population: Unresectable HCC amenable to TACE, no extrahepatic disease, Child-Pugh A–B7; Vp3/Vp4 excluded. BCLC A 26% / B 57% / C 16%; beyond up-to-7 52%; PVI (Vp1–2) 7%.
treatment: TACE + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w → durvalumab 1120 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w (bevacizumab only ≥14 d after last TACE) vs TACE + durvalumab + placebo vs TACE + placebo
endpoints: ⏳ Not reported (interim OS not significant; still masked)
takeaway: First positive phase 3 of systemic therapy plus TACE: durvalumab + bevacizumab + TACE improved PFS to 15.0 vs 8.2 months (HR 0.77). Durvalumab alone + TACE did not help, suggesting the anti-VEGF partner matters; OS has not yet been reported.

name: RUBY
population: Primary advanced stage III–IV (not amenable to cure) or first-recurrence endometrial cancer; carcinosarcoma allowed. dMMR/MSI-H 24%; recurrent 48%, primary stage IV 34%, stage III 19%.
treatment: Dostarlimab 500 mg + CP q3w ×6 → dostarlimab 1000 mg q6w (≤3 yr) vs placebo + CP → placebo
takeaway: Dostarlimab added to carboplatin-paclitaxel (CP) and continued as maintenance improved PFS in first-line advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer: dMMR HR 0.28 (24-mo PFS 61% vs 16%), overall HR 0.64. The benefit is smaller in pMMR (PFS HR 0.76); OS looks favourable (HR 0.64) but is interim and the boundary was not crossed.

name: CREATE-X
population: HER2-negative stage I–IIIB breast cancer with residual disease (non-pCR, or ypN+) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Japan and South Korea. HR+ 68%, TNBC 32%; stage IIIA–IIIB ~40%.
treatment: Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID D1–14 Q3W ×6–8 cycles + standard therapy vs standard therapy alone
takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine for 6–8 cycles in HER2-negative breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy improved both DFS and OS. The benefit was concentrated in TNBC; the HR+ subgroup showed no significant benefit.

name: PACIFIC
population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC (IASLC 7th) without progression after ≥2 cycles of platinum-based chemoradiation. Unselected for PD-L1 (TC ≥25% 22%, <25% 41%, unknown 37%); EGFR-mutant 6%.
treatment: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg Q2W for up to 12 mo vs placebo (2:1); consolidation starting 1–42 days after chemoRT
takeaway: One year of consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiation improved PFS and OS and became standard of care. Benefit was seen regardless of PD-L1 but was smaller in EGFR-mutant disease, and treatment should start within 14 days after chemoradiation.

name: AMPLITUDE
population: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC); HRD required. BRCA1/2 56%, high volume 78%, prior docetaxel 16%.
treatment: Niraparib 200 mg + abiraterone 1000 mg (dual-action tablet) + prednisone 5 mg QD vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone (AAP)
takeaway: Niraparib + abiraterone-prednisone improved rPFS over abiraterone-prednisone in HRR-positive mCSPC, but OS is immature. The benefit is concentrated in BRCA (non-BRCA HR 0.81, post hoc); anemia and hypertension were notable toxicities.

name: ATHENA-MONO
population: FIGO III–IV HGSC/EC, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer, regardless of HRD status. CR ~55%, stage III 76%, HRD 43%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs placebo (4:1), up to 2 years
endpoints: ITT 48.8% vs 9.1%; HRD 58.8% vs 20.0% (not formally tested)
takeaway: Rucaparib maintenance in first line improved PFS in HRD-positive disease, the ITT population (HR 0.52) and HRD-negative disease (HR 0.65). It covers the broadest first-line PARPi population (R0 resection allowed, 79% BRCA wild-type), though OS is immature.

name: EMERALD-3
population: Embolisation-eligible unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A, no Vp3/Vp4; ≤1 prior palliative embolisation. BCLC A 20% / B 62% / C 18%; beyond up-to-7 62%; Asian 72%.
treatment: STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w) + lenvatinib 8/12 mg QD + TACE vs STRIDE + TACE vs TACE alone (open-label, sponsor-blinded)
endpoints: 12.9 vs 8.1 mo (first 175) — HR 0.71 (0.56–0.91), not formally tested
NR vs 32.9 mo — HR 0.70 (0.51–0.95), not formally tested
ORR 37% vs 30% (STRIDE+TACE 41% vs 27%); DCR 79% vs 66% (STRIDE+TACE 74% vs 61%)
takeaway: STRIDE + lenvatinib + TACE improved PFS (13.0 vs 9.8 mo, HR 0.70), but the OS HR of 0.84 was not significant at interim. STRIDE + TACE without lenvatinib looked as good (PFS HR 0.71, OS HR 0.70) with less toxicity, but was not formally tested; lenvatinib added G3–4 TRAEs, discontinuations and deaths.

name: IMvigor130
population: Both cisplatin-eligible and -ineligible patients. Carboplatin 70% (A) / 66% (C); UTUC 27%. Arm B restricted to IC2/3 after Apr 2018.
treatment: Atezolizumab + platinum-gemcitabine (A) vs atezolizumab monotherapy (B) vs placebo + platinum-gemcitabine (C)
endpoints: ❌ 15.2 vs 13.3 mo — HR 0.98 (0.82–1.16), not formally tested
A vs C: ORR 48.1% vs 44.8%, DCR 65% vs 60%; B vs C: ORR 24.2% vs 44.4%, DCR 38% vs 59%
takeaway: PFS was positive but final OS was not (A vs C HR 0.85). Atezolizumab monotherapy OS was about equal to chemotherapy in the ITT population, with a signal only in PD-L1 IC2/3 cisplatin-ineligible patients (HR 0.56, post hoc). In the cisplatin subgroup OS was 21.5 vs 13.4 mo (HR 0.76, exploratory), which supports a cisplatin-based ICI combination.

name: MITO END-2
population: Advanced (FIGO III–IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer, measurable or evaluable; ≤1 prior platinum line (≥6 mo interval); carcinosarcoma excluded; ECOG ≤2. Recurrent ~62%, G3 ~50%, serous/clear cell 16%, prior chemo 24%.
treatment: Carboplatin-paclitaxel (CP) + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab maintenance vs CP (carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 q3w ×6–8)
takeaway: Bevacizumab + CP in advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer missed its primary PFS endpoint, with numerically higher ORR, 6-month DCR and OS. It added thromboembolism, hypertension and discontinuations, and this was a small phase II trial without molecular stratification.

name: TALAPRO-3
population: mCSPC with HRD. BRCA1/2 35%; de novo 84%, high volume 71%. ≤3 mo prior ADT ± ARPI allowed; no prior docetaxel.
treatment: Talazoparib 0.5 mg QD + enzalutamide vs placebo + enzalutamide (+ ADT)
endpoints: ⏳ NR vs NR — HR 0.77 (0.56–1.04), NS (boundary not crossed); 3-yr 78% vs 72%
ORR 75% vs 67%; DCR 97% vs 94% (CR+PR+SD, derived from Fig. 3D)
takeaway: Talazoparib + enzalutamide improved rPFS (HR 0.48) over enzalutamide in HRR-mutated mHSPC, with benefit in both BRCA and non-BRCA subgroups. OS is immature (interim HR 0.77, not significant), and grade ≥3 anemia occurred in 51%.

name: CARES-005
population: Unresectable HCC treatable with TACE (CNLC Ib–IIIa = BCLC A–C without extrahepatic mets), Child-Pugh A; China only. BCLC C 43%, PVTT Vp3–4 27%, beyond up-to-7 90%, HBV 80%.
treatment: TACE + camrelizumab 200 mg q3w + rivoceranib (apatinib) 250 mg QD vs TACE alone (on-demand cTACE; crossover allowed at progression)
endpoints: ✅ 10.8 vs 3.2 mo — HR 0.34 (0.24–0.50), P<0.001 (composite: RECICL + CP-C + TACE failure/refractoriness)
⏳ 24.0 vs 21.5 mo — HR 0.87 (0.57–1.32), P=0.50; immature (90 deaths), 75% of TACE-arm progressors crossed over
takeaway: TACE plus camrelizumab and rivoceranib improved PFS to 10.8 vs 3.2 months (HR 0.34) over TACE alone, and is the only TACE-combination trial enrolling BCLC C / Vp3–4 PVTT patients (27%). OS is immature and confounded by 75% crossover; this is a phase II, open-label, investigator-assessed, China-only trial.

name: GOG-229E
population: Recurrent/persistent endometrial cancer after 1–2 prior cytotoxic regimens; measurable disease, GOG PS 0–2, no prior VEGF-targeted therapy. Serous 27%, grade 3 71%, 2 prior regimens 37%.
treatment: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w (single-arm, no control)
takeaway: Single-agent bevacizumab in second- and third-line endometrial cancer met its 6-month PFS criterion (40%, best among GOG historical controls) but ORR was only 13.5%, with responses across histologies (4/7 serous). High plasma VEGF-A was associated with no response and worse OS (exploratory).

name: LEAP-012
population: Unresectable, non-metastatic HCC amenable to TACE; no PVI or extrahepatic disease; CP-A. Tumour ≥10 cm, >10 tumours or ≥50% of liver excluded. BCLC A 31% / B 59% / C 10%; tumour burden score ≤6 48%.
treatment: Lenvatinib 8/12 mg QD + pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (≤2 yr) + TACE vs dual placebo + TACE; systemic therapy started 2–4 wk before first TACE
endpoints: ⚠️ Median not reported; 24-mo 75% vs 69% — HR 0.80 (0.57–1.11), P=0.087 (IA; boundary 0.0012)
takeaway: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab + TACE improved PFS to 14.6 vs 10.0 months (HR 0.66), but OS (a dual primary endpoint) was not significant at interim and the trial later announced closure for low likelihood of meeting the OS threshold. Toxicity was heavy, with grade ≥3 TRAEs in 71%.

name: RADIANT-2
population: Functional (G1–2) GI-NET with PD within 1 yr. Small intestine 52%, lung 10%, colon 7%; prior SSA 79%, prior ChT 30%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs placebo + octreotide LAR 30 mg q28d
takeaway: Everolimus in functional GI-NET missed the PFS significance boundary on central review and showed no OS benefit (58% crossover). This led to RADIANT-4 in non-functional NETs.

name: KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304
population: Cisplatin-eligible MIBC (cT2–T4aN0 or T1–T4aN1), ECOG 0–1. T3N0/T4aN0 ~72%; CPS ≥10 ~57%.
treatment: EV-P (neoadjuvant ×4 → surgery → adjuvant EV ×5 + P ×13) vs cis-gem (neoadjuvant ×4) → surgery
takeaway: EFS, OS and pCR were all positive versus cis-gem neoadjuvant chemo, making this the first non-platinum regimen to beat cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemo. Together with KN-905, it supports peri-operative EV-P regardless of cisplatin eligibility. Caveats: the control arm had no peri-operative ICI (cf. NIAGARA), and the experimental arm had more adverse events and longer treatment.

name: AcceleRET-Lung
population: Treatment-naive RET fusion-positive mNSCLC, ECOG 0–1. Europe 71%; history of CNS metastases 28%. Terminated by sponsor at 98.7% accrual.
treatment: Pralsetinib (n=110) vs platinum-based chemo ± pembrolizumab (n=113)
takeaway: First-line pralsetinib beat platinum chemo on PFS (18.7 vs 9.0 mo), ORR and DoR. Caution: an infection signal (fatal 7.4%) led to a protocol amendment in October 2024 to strengthen monitoring; OS is immature with 34% crossover.

name: GOG0209
population: Chemo-naive stage III/IV or recurrent endometrial cancer with poor potential for cure by surgery/RT; GOG PS 0–2. Measurable or recurrent 61%; non-measurable stage III/IV allowed from 2006.
treatment: Paclitaxel 175 + carboplatin AUC 6 (TC) q3w ×7 vs TAP (doxorubicin 45 + cisplatin 50 d1, paclitaxel 160 d2 + G-CSF) q3w ×7
takeaway: Carboplatin + paclitaxel was non-inferior to TAP for OS and PFS, with less toxicity and slightly better QoL. TC became the first-line standard for advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer and the backbone for later ICI trials (GY018, RUBY, DUO-E).

name: LIBRETTO-001
population: RET fusion-positive NSCLC / thyroid cancer; RET-mutant MTC; other RET fusion-positive solid tumors (tumor-agnostic). N=796 (all cohorts).
treatment: Selpercatinib 160 mg BID (single-arm, multi-cohort basket)
endpoints: ✅ Thyroid (non-MTC): naive 96%, pretreated 85%; MTC: cabo/vande-naive 81%, pretreated 76%
takeaway: Selpercatinib produced high response rates across RET fusion NSCLC, thyroid cancer and RET-mutant MTC, leading to FDA approval in 2020 and a tumor-agnostic approval in September 2022. Responses were poorer in colorectal cancer (ORR 20%, DoR 9.4 mo); the study is single-arm with no hazard ratios.

name: NCT01367002 (HER2+ USC)
population: HER2+ (IHC 3+ or 2+/FISH+) uterine serous carcinoma, stage III–IV after surgery (71%) or measurable recurrent (29%; PFI >6 mo, ≤3 prior ChT); ECOG 0–2. Central HER2 review. Control arm older (median 73 vs 66).
treatment: CP + trastuzumab (8 → 6 mg/kg q3w) ×6 → trastuzumab maintenance until PD vs CP (carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 q3w ×6)
takeaway: Trastuzumab added to CP in HER2+ uterine serous carcinoma improved PFS (HR 0.46) and OS (HR 0.58) with no added toxicity. The largest benefit was in stage III–IV primary disease (OS NR vs 25.4 mo), with no OS gain in recurrent disease. Caveat: small phase II (n=58), one-sided α 0.10 with 90% CIs, closed early for slow accrual.

name: RADIANT-3
population: Grade 1–2 pNET with progressive disease within 1 yr. Well differentiated 83%; liver metastases 92%; functional 24%. Prior chemo 50%, prior SSA 49%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily vs placebo, both with best supportive care (SSA allowed)
takeaway: Everolimus improved PFS in progressive pNET and is standard of care in second line. Most disease stabilized rather than responded, OS was confounded by 73% crossover, and side effects included stomatitis, hyperglycemia and ILD.

name: SOLO-1
population: FIGO III–IV; HGSC/EC, fallopian/peritoneal cancer; BRCA1/2 mutated. Prior bevacizumab excluded. CR 82%, stage III 83%, BRCA1 72%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs placebo (2:1) up to 2 years (longer if PR)
takeaway: Olaparib maintenance in first line after AD TC in BRCA-mutated disease improved PFS, with benefit sustained after the 2-year stop. OS did not reach the formal significance threshold (p=.0004 vs 0.0001).
